News.title: Fix palliative care before assisted dying debate, says PM
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said that before assisted dying is considered in England and Wales, the funding of palliative and social care should be "fixed".

It is the first time Burnham has set out his position on the issue since becoming prime minister, as MPs prepare to debate it again when Parliament returns in September.

The government is likely to remain officially neutral, but Burnham's remarks suggest he personally will not back a bill being proposed by Labour MP Lauren Edwards.

The position is a shift from that of former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, who voted in favour of the previous attempt to legalise assisted dying and gave time for the issue to be debated in Parliament.

Sir Keir's support was privately cited by some Labour MPs as a reason they backed the bill last time.

Burnham told reporters: "I take the view that that debate - and I don't say that there shouldn't be a debate at some point about those issues - personally, I think there's something that needs to happen first.

"That is the fixing of the funding of palliative care and social care.

"I think it is very challenging to introduce that wider debate in a context of people not receiving that care and having the peace of mind about that care."

In 2025, MPs voted in favour of a bill proposed by Labour MP Kim Leadbeater to legalise assisted dying.

But the bill was not passed by the House of Lords, after an unprecedented number of suggested amendments delayed its progress until it ran out of time in April this year.

Its opponents argued it had substantial flaws that risked vulnerable people being pressured into ending their lives early.

The proposed law - known as the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - would have allowed people over the age of 18 who were expected to die within six months to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

Labour MP Lauren Edwards plans to bring forward an identical bill in order to "finish the job" started by Leadbeater.

Following Burnham's comments, she said improving social care and legalising assisted dying was "not a case of either/or" and that the two things "can and must go hand in hand".

"The bill that has been before Parliament and thoroughly debated since October 2024 provides for a four-year implementation period - that means if my current bill becomes law next year, we would have until 2031 to fix the status quo that Andy Burnham rightly says is broken."

Jess Asato - a Labour MP and opponent of the bill - said MPs had "a responsibility to consider the safety of introducing such a flawed bill into a broken and failing care system".

"There can be no meaningful choice and no dignity at the end of life if we don't have a palliative care system that provides basic support for the vulnerable and an affordable social care system that gives everyone dignity at the end of their lives."

Burnham was asked about his views on assisted dying after he had announced plans to reform the social care system, with the view to create a national care service and to reach a political consensus on how to fund it.

In 2024, just before the first Commons vote on the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, Burnham told BBC Manchester he would "probably vote in favour of it" if he was in Parliament.

When he was previously an MP he abstained from a 2015 vote on another bill to legalise assisted dying because of concerns over safeguards and people feeling under pressure.

But he told the BBC in 2024 that he had had "family experience in the nine years since that has changed my view".

He said: "I think we do allow people to suffer and families to suffer too much."

He caveated his support as being for the principle of assisted dying and insisted he would want a requirement before any new law was implemented that hospices would be "properly funded and sorted out".

News.title: Body of Scottish woman found inside suitcase in Greece
News.content:
The body of a Scottish woman has been found inside a suitcase in an abandoned building in Greece, prompting a multi-agency investigation.

Police Scotland confirmed they are liaising with authorities after the woman was reportedly discovered by a homeless man in the Kypseli district in Athens on 18 July.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, is thought to have travelled to Greece from Cyprus last month, state broadcaster ERT reports. She is believed to have died between five and seven days before she was found.

Greek police told BBC Scotland News the body of a British woman was found and fingerprint data from Interpol matched a woman born in 1988. Investigations are ongoing.

News.title: Amy Winehouse's dad ordered to pay £1m by court
News.content:
Amy Winehouse's father must pay just under Â£1m to two of his daughter's friends after a failed High Court claim over the auctioning of the late singer's items.

Mitch Winehouse also racked up at least Â£950,000 in his own legal costs in the failed attempt against Naomi Parry and Catriona Gourlay.

He claimed the women had profited from selling dozens of his daughter's items at auctions in the US in 2021 and 2023, accusing them of having "deliberately concealed" their sale.

But Ms Justice Clarke threw out the claim earlier this year, finding that he "knew all along" about the intended sale and only afterwards had begun to pursue them for money in an "aggressive and unpleasant way".

In a judgment on Wednesday, she said: "The claimant chose to bring an inherently weak claim, pursue it aggressively and relentlessly to the end, and make serious and unfounded allegations against the defendants which significantly damaged their reputations, career prospects, financial security and health."

News.title: Boy, 7, dies in hospital after beach tragedy
News.content:
A seven-year-old boy has died in hospital after a beach tragedy that also killed his teenage cousin and her mother, his family has said.

Musa Ahmed was on a day trip to West Mersea, Essex, on 22 July, when he and five relatives got into difficulty in the water.

While he was pulled from the water and airlifted to hospital, Shelina Rahman, 41, and 15-year-old Sameeha, died at the scene.

Musa's family said he died "in a state of ease and peace" at the Royal London Hospital on Tuesday evening.

The family had travelled to the island, near Colchester, from Barking in east London that morning.

Three others were also taken to hospital by ambulance after the incident, first reported to Essex Police at 17:35 BST, and were said by the force to be "recovering".

Musa's father, Shahin Ahmed, has said they were swept away by a "very strong" tide and police said they made "significant efforts to help each other".

Posting on Facebook earlier, Ahmed said of his son: "He made every person feel special and never failed to bring happiness."

News.title: Man accused of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor threat faces December trial
News.content:
A man charged with threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor near his home on the Sandringham Estate in Norfolk will stand trial in December.

Alex Jenkinson, 39, is accused of causing the former Duke of York to "fear unlawful violence" during an encounter as he walked his dogs on 6 May.

The trial - which will begin on 21 December - is expected to include evidence from Mountbatten-Windsor via videolink.

Jenkinson is accused of using threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour and had been due to stand trial on Wednesday. At Westminster Magistrates' Court, chief magistrate Paul Goldspring postponed proceedings over concerns about the defendant's mental health.

News.title: Chief constable resigns before misconduct tribunal
News.content:
The chief constable of Staffordshire Police has resigned, ahead of a gross misconduct hearing regarding his behaviour.

Chris Noble was suspended in August amid inquiries by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), with the watchdog confirming in March that it had opened two more investigations regarding his behaviour.

Noble resigned on Tuesday via a letter to the Police and Crime Commissioner for Staffordshire, Ben Adams.

The misconduct hearing began on Wednesday morning in Noble's absence and has since been adjourned.

He was chosen to lead Staffordshire Police after the retirement of the previous chief constable in 2021.

Prior to this, he was the assistant chief constable of Humberside Police.

In a statement, Staffordshire Commissioner for Police, Fire & Rescue and Crime, Ben Adams said: "I can confirm that yesterday [28 July], I received Chief Constable Chris Noble's resignation, which I have accepted with immediate effect.

"Becky Riggs will remain as Staffordshire Police's acting chief constable.

"The misconduct hearing will continue today as planned, under former officer provisions."

Staffordshire Police said that it would not be appropriate to comment due to ongoing misconduct proceedings.

In a recent statement, the IOPC said: "The chair of the panel has directed that no additional information relating to the detail of the allegations can be released at this time.

"We are continuing to investigate other allegations relating to Mr Noble. Given the sensitivity of those matters, for operational reasons, no further information can be provided at this time."

Do you ever see your cat shifting his front paws back and forth just before settling down for a nap? Have you heard some cat lovers talk about their feline friends “making biscuits” or “kneading dough”?

Scientists who study cat behavior call this distinctive paw action “kneading” and believe it to be a sign of a relaxed cat. My own cats knead before taking a nap near me. While they are kneading, they purr – one of them gets so relaxed, he sometimes drools. Kneading usually occurs near a favorite person.

As a veterinarian, I think it’s important to recognize the little moments your cat is telling you she’s happy to be near you.

open image in gallery Scientists who study cat behavior call this distinctive paw action ‘kneading’ and believe it to be a sign of a relaxed cat ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

At the same time, the kitten usually purrs, which is a sound created by rapid vibrations of certain throat muscles. Purring is a signal for attention.

Using these two behaviors, kittens are asking their moms, also known as queens, to remain still so they can continue suckling. Young kittens usually fall asleep while suckling.

Kittens stop drinking their mother’s milk by about two months of age. So why do cats continue to knead as adults?

Ready to relax

Kneading seems to be more common in some cats than others. If your cat doesn’t knead, it could mean he is a little stressed – or it could just be that your cat doesn’t display relaxation or affection in that manner.

But many cats do continue kneading into adulthood. It’s pretty safe to assume a cat who is kneading is feeling calm, content and ready to settle down, just like a kitten settling in to suckle and sleep.

You may already know that when your cat bunts, or butts his head and rubs his cheek, head and body against your leg or an object near you, he is putting his scent in these locations. Cats also have scent glands between their toes, prompting some people to suggest that cats are also putting a familiar, comforting scent on their sleeping area when they knead.

About the author Julia Albright is an Associate Professor of Veterinary Medicine, University of Tennessee. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Don’t bother to look for these glands on your own cat. They are not easily visible.

Subtle signals

Kneading may also be a form of communication between cats and their people.

If you’ve been around dogs, you know most are quite obvious in letting humans know they want something or like someone. For thousands of years, people have purposely bred dogs to be fun companions, as well as to have useful behaviors such as herding, tracking or guarding.

Cats and people have also lived together for thousands of years – and humans have appreciated their amazing natural mousing skills. Only recently have people tried to breed cats, but mostly for their appearance, not for specific behaviors.

The result is that cats are a little more subtle than dogs in their ways of telling a person, “I like you.” Kneading is one of those clues.

Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has hit “crisis-era lows”, a UK-based maritime data firm has reported as a brief pause in fighting was shattered by fresh clashes in the Middle East.

Lloyd’s List Intelligence said amid the worsening security situation “a near-term recovery in traffic” through the strategic waterway was unlikely.

The disruption to trade through the Gulf channel, which is a vital oil and gas supply route, has driven up fuel and food prices.

In an update, Lloyd’s said initial figures showed there were just 39 vessel transits from July 20-26, down from 82 the previous week.

This represents only a fraction of the traffic before the war, when on average nearly 140 ships a day made the crossing.

open image in gallery The US president says Iran will be hit ‘hard’ (Paul Sancya/AP) ( AP )

The monitor said: “The deteriorating security environment in the Strait of Hormuz has driven vessel traffic back to crisis-era lows.”

It added: “A near-term recovery in traffic is unlikely. Neither Tehran nor Washington has shifted position materially, leaving owners reluctant to resume normal trading patterns.”

Meanwhile, the renewed hostilities have threatened to expand the conflict.

A US-owned gas storage tanker in the Egyptian port of Damietta in the eastern Mediterranean was struck by a drone, according to the British maritime security firm Ambrey.

It came after Iran launched missiles at US forces in the Middle East as the American military joined with Saudi Arabia in attacking Tehran-backed militias in neighbouring Iraq.

The latest violence was triggered by what the Pentagon described as “an attempted surprise attack” by Tehran on US personnel based in the region, which it said was successfully intercepted.

Having previously halted an intensive 13-day military offensive against Iran, Donald Trump was quoted by Fox News as saying: “We’ll be hitting them hard. We’re going to beat the f****** shit out of them.”

open image in gallery (PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

Before the new flare-up, mediators had expressed hope about bringing the US and Iran back to the negotiating table.

An interim ceasefire deal collapsed in recent weeks after renewed fighting in the contested Strait of Hormuz, which has been a flashpoint in the war.

Iran has continued to try to maintain its stranglehold on the channel, which had been open before the US and Israel began the conflict, including demanding ships seek permission to transit, attacking vessels and threatening to impose charges.

In response, the US has moved to crack down on bodies backed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) “for running coercive ‘insurance’ schemes that extort international shipping transiting the Strait of Hormuz”.

State department spokesman Tommy Piggott said: “These entities manufacture risk – including the threat of vessel seizures – and then charge commercial vessels for coverage against dangers created by the regime itself, generating revenue that sustains IRGC operations and Iran’s broader campaign of regional destabilisation.”

The police chief from St. Paul, Minnesota, has accused the city’s mayor of sexual harassment against him and other city employees, including sending a message wishing a “Happy Weiner Wednesday!”

The city has been put on notice that Mayor Kaohly Her “has engaged in illegal conduct towards city employees,” Chris Madel, a lawyer for Police Chief Axel Henry, wrote in an April 1 letter to St. Paul City Attorney Irene Kao, as reported by local media.

The letter included a screenshot of a text message allegedly sent by Her to an unnamed city worker that read, “Happy Weiner Wednesday! Wish I was having a [hot dog emoji] with you all on 6 today!”

Below the message is a partially redacted photo of what appears to be a swaddled baby with the caption, “When she wraps you up in her blanket after you gave her a good weinering,” with two laughing emojis, according to the Minnesota Star Tribune and KARE 11.

The redacted part of the photo was the face of a St. Paul police officer on Her’s security team superimposed on the baby, a person familiar with the matter told the Star Tribune.

open image in gallery The police chief has accused St. Paul Mayor Kaohly Her of sexual harassment, including sending a message wishing a ‘Happy Weiner Wednesday!’ ( Getty )

The term “Weiner Wednesdays” has been coined by some employees for a weekly event where a civilian worker brings in hot dogs for some St. Paul Police Department staff, according to the Star Tribune’s sources.

While the mayor’s office did not comment on the specific allegations, a spokesperson for Her said, “The mayor has deep respect for city employees and regrets any unintended impact her actions may have had.”

When reached for further comment, Madel said Chief Henry “just helped crack a triple homicide in under four hours — that's the work he's focused on right now: keeping citizens safe.”

Henry decided to file a formal complaint after “becoming aware that the Mayor’s conduct has extended beyond isolated incidents and has included sexual harassment of subordinate City employees, including members of the Saint Paul Police Department,” Madel wrote in his letter.

open image in gallery St. Paul has been put on notice that Mayor Kaohly Her ‘has engaged in illegal conduct towards city employees,’ a lawyer for Police Chief Axel Henry said ( Getty Images )

The attorney has demanded the city “immediately take all steps necessary” to extract data from Her’s phones.

Madel warned in the letter that litigation is “reasonably foreseeable.”

The Independent has reached out to the mayor’s office for comment.

The city of St. Paul has hired an outside law firm to investigate the sexual harassment claims against Her, who was elected as the first woman mayor last fall, according to the Star Tribune.

The person familiar with the matter who spoke with the publication said sexualized communications and unwanted physical contact from Her directed at Henry are included in the probe.

The Metropolitan Police has said no further action will be taken against Green Party leader Zack Polanski over a picture shared on social media.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage reported Mr Polanski to the police after he shared an image depicting a man wearing a black T-shirt with a picture of a guillotine and the words: “We’re only making plans for Nigel.”

But in a statement on Wednesday, the Met said it would not be pursuing the case as “an extensive investigation was deemed to be disproportionate and not a reasonable use of police resources”.

A Reform UK spokesperson criticised the police’s decision to take no further action against Mr Polanski, saying: “Once again we see that we are living in two-tier Britain.”

The force said a crime should be recorded in relation to the wearing of the T-shirt, and as that happened in Bristol, the case has been transferred to Avon and Somerset Police to consider what further action should follow.

open image in gallery Green Party leader Zack Polanski said he ‘made a mistake’ over a social media post ( Rich McCarthy/PA )

A statement from the Met said: “Officers have reviewed the reports, giving careful consideration to whether further action should follow. That review reached the following conclusions:

“It is unlikely that the sharing of the image online would constitute a criminal offence. Officers have considered telecommunications, public order and other offences, including incitement, in reaching this conclusion.

“The image in question was the 18th in a post containing 20 images. The person named on the reports received has stated publicly, either directly or in statements issued on his behalf, that he had not seen the specific image in question when he accepted the invitation to collaborate.

open image in gallery Reform UK leader Nigel Farage reported Mr Polanski to the police ( PA Wire )

“Steps were taken to remove the post from his account when the issue was raised.

“The post has since been shared (whether by collaboration, reposting or sharing) by around 130 accounts. The image has additionally been shared on many more occasions on other social media platforms.

“We must not treat individuals differently solely because of their public profile, and therefore any investigation would need to have considered not just the actions of the individual named in the reports, but of all 130+ people and organisations.

“Given it is unlikely their actions would have ultimately constituted an offence, such an extensive investigation was deemed to do be disproportionate and not a reasonable use of police resources.

“Accordingly, no further action will be taken in relation to the sharing of the image online.”

More to follow...

Growing up about 20 miles south of the Irish Hills, Nathan Wakefield was a regular visitor to “ southern Michigan’s vacation land.”

The region along US 12 was filled with roadside attractions, where kids like Wakefield could climb towers, traverse a prehistoric forest and see blacksmiths and saloons in scenes that mimicked Western films.

Today, most of those roadside stops in Jackson and Lenawee counties have disappeared, casualties of changing tourism preferences and a steady decline in traffic after I-94 diverted motorists from what had been a primary route between Detroit and Chicago.

One of Wakefield’s favorites still stands, though, and this year, he bought it: Mystery Hill, known for its gravity-defying house, and the three acres it sits on.

It’s an attempt to encourage “generational nostalgia,” the Adrian native told Bridge Michigan, noting he did not want the attraction to go the way of others that have fallen into disrepair or long ago closed.

“I’m just elated to be a part of this ongoing legacy,” Wakefield added.

Mystery Hill is one of the few remaining roadside attractions in the Irish Hills, a region that still attracts tourists for its natural beauty and the Michigan International Speedway.

The area was once home to Frontier City and Stagecoach Stop, roadside attractions that had a bank, blacksmith, general store, jailhouse, livery stable and saloon, all popular establishments featured in popular Western films.

They closed in 1974 and 2007, respectively.

With new technology increasingly competing for attention, roadside attractions that remain viable “offer full-body experiences like putt-putt golf or go-kart racing” — things people “can’t do virtually,” said Michelle McLemore, one of the historians for Cambridge Township in the Irish Hills.

“At Mystery Hill, you can … go inside, explore the building to see and feel the craziness with the gravity,” McLemore said.

Prehistoric Forest, a dinosaur-themed amusement park in the area, also met its demise in 2002 and was left abandoned until 2019, when Sandra Crabb, who grew up in Dearborn, purchased it with hopes to restore the park.

The restoration never happened, and now, the Irish Hills Print Co. is operating on the property, according to the Cambridge Township Clerk.

One of the reasons Mystery Hill was able to stand the test of time is that it doesn’t have as much overhead as some of the other roadside attractions, McLemore said. “They don’t require as many people to employ … or a bunch of food vendors,” she added.

Nearby Bauer Manor, along US 12, had served as a fine-dining restaurant where customers could enjoy a “fancy” meal while overlooking Evans Lake. It closed in 2003.

Unlike many of the roadside attractions he remembers from childhood, Mystery Hill remained remarkably well preserved, something Wakefield noticed immediately when he returned for a visit last year.

“I left thinking, ‘Wow, it’d be nice to own something like this,’” he recalled. “I’m surprised it’s in such good condition. I’m glad somebody swooped in and kind of kept the legacy going.”

That somebody was Dirk Dole, of California, who purchased Mystery Hill in 2022 and added an oddities museum and a gemstone mining experience.

“He’ll buy these roadside attractions, fix them up, and flip them, and then sell them to locals that are really passionate and can run them,” Wakefield said.

“Between my business acumen as well as my show business background, it just felt like a total perfect match.”

For the past 15 years, Wakefield has worked as a professional sideshow artist, performing stunts like lying on a bed of nails, juggling and eating fire. He said he wants to bring experiences like that to Mystery Hill.

“I’ve seen this firsthand: So many people show up with their kids or their grandkids, and they say, ‘Man, I remember coming here when I was a kid, and so I just had to bring my kids or my grandkids to check it out,’” Wakefield said.

He plans to continue operating the famous gravitational house tours that have made Mystery Hill a destination for generations, but he also hopes to transform the property into a broader family entertainment destination.

His emphasis on nostalgia and family experiences aligns with messaging from Pure Michigan, the state’s tourism arm.

“As new generations of travelers are looking to both create new memories and revisit familiar stops when planning their vacations, attractions like Mystery Hill in Irish Hills add to the unique yet nostalgic experiences that are waiting to be discovered throughout Michigan’s two peninsulas,” said Vice President Kelly Wolgamott.

Zendaya traded gothic glamour for shimmering spider-webs as she arrived at the London premiere of Spider-Man: Brand New Day in London.

The actress wore a couture ivory Tamara Ralph gown, featuring a sculpted bodice and mermaid tail draped in delicate crystal threads to mimic the gossamer strands of a spider’s web.

Rather than relying on the superhero’s signature red-and-blue palette or gothic all-black looks she’s sported at earlier premieres, Wednesday’s ensemble wove the film’s central motif more subtly into the construction of the dress.

open image in gallery Zendaya in Tmara Ralph (Doug Peters/PA)

The 29-year-old’s hair and beauty choices were a noticeable departure from the styling at the Los Angeles premiere on Tuesday night. Gone were the dramatic wet-look “spider bangs” that mimicked spiders’ legs. Instead, Zendaya wore her hair in loose, voluminous natural waves.

Tom Holland, who plays Spider-Man, wore a burgundy Louis Vuitton suit with a matching tie and statement spider brooch. The couple have harmonised their red carpet looks throughout this press tour, following the announcement by Holland during an interview with Esquire in June that they had married.

open image in gallery Tom Holland and Zendaya at the London premiere (Ian West/PA)

Zendaya, who plays Michelle Jones-Watson, the love interest of Spider-Man’s alter-ego Peter Parker, has become almost as famous for dressing for her films as she has for starring in them, thanks to the vision of her stylist Law Roach, including red carpet looks for films such as Challengers, Dune: Part Two and The Odyssey.

For the Los Angeles premiere on July 27, Zendaya embraced the darker side of the Spider-Man universe in a black satin corset dress by Ashi Studio, complete with antennae and surrounded by sweeping pleats and an imposing architectural train.

open image in gallery Zendaya wearing Ashi Studio at the LA premiere (Alamy/PA)

Celebrity hairstylist Ursula Stephen extended the theme through Zendaya’s beauty look, styling her fringe into wet-look “spider bangs” that tapered across her forehead to resemble spindly legs.

But London isn’t the first time Zendaya has leaned into understatement on this press tour. In Berlin, she wore a custom black Louis Vuitton leather two-piece made up of a cropped vest and low-slung skirt.

open image in gallery Zendaya at the Spider-Man: Brand New Day press day in Berlin (Alamy/PA)

Rather than building the Spider-Man references into the clothing itself, the storytelling came through the accessories. Oversized Lydia Courteille spider-web earrings, set with sapphires, aquamarines and tanzanites, were paired with a co-ordinating ring, while make-up artist Ernesto Casillas revealed he created deliberately “spidery” lashes to echo the jewellery.

In Rome, Zendaya also had spider-webs woven throughout her dress while dipping into the archives in a sheer black Giorgio Armani gown from the designer’s spring 1990 collection.

Silver cobweb-like beading stretched across the sheer fabric and nude underlay, making the connection with Spider-Man rather less subtle. Roach shared on Instagram that he and Zendaya “only wear Italian when in Italy”, although the jewellery was from the decidedly New York Tiffany & Co.

In Mexico City, the arachnid dressing continued with a more gothic approach when Zendaya wore an asymmetric black Ashi Studio couture gown combining smooth black fabric with intricate web-like detailing across one side of the body. Long strands of fringe fell towards the floor like trailing webs, while Jacob & Co spider earrings cemented the motif.

open image in gallery Zendaya attending the red carpet for Spider-Man: A New Day in Mexico (Alamy/PA)

Her towering bouffant hairstyle, reminiscent of Audrey Hepburn in Breakfast at Tiffany’s, brought a touch of the swinging Sixties to the otherwise dark and moody look.

Across the promotional tour, Zendaya and Roach have interpreted the same superhero through remarkably different lenses: from custom leather to delicate archival threads.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day, follows a solitary Peter Parker four years after the events of No Way Home. As Spider-Man (Holland) struggles with loneliness and a visceral physical mutation, he must stop a mind-controlling threat alongside The Punisher and The Hulk.

The film is released in UK cinemas on July 31.

News.title: Baroness Casey calls for benefits overhaul: ‘Even I would qualify as disabled’
News.content:
Baroness Casey has called for an overhaul to the benefits system as she claimed that she would “qualify as disabled” as it currently stands.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Wednesday (29 July), Casey, who is leading a review into social care, said that we must ask “who should we be looking after, and how”.

Casey explained that according to an official survey by the Department of Work and Pensions, 16.8 million people had self-reported a disability in the 2023-24 financial year, equating to a quarter of the country.

“I don’t buy it,” she said.

“I would qualify, and I’m sitting here right now. I’m not disabled, but I could qualify if I answered those questions based on my medical records, it’s simple as.”

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola transfer: Liverpool ready £110m bid as PSG star approves Anfield move
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola transfer: Liverpool ready £110m bid as PSG star approves Anfield move

Liverpool are still searching for Mohamed Salah’s replacement but they appear to have been handed encouragement in their interest in PSG and France forward Bradley Barcola

View 2 Images PSG have set a high price for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are readying their opening offer for Bradley Barcola with the winger open to a move to Anfield - but PSG are remaining firm over their asking price. The Reds have identified the French forward as an ideal option to bolster their forward line following Mohamed Salah’s exit.

‌



Barcola had been mentioned alongside a host of other names including Yan Diomande, who now appears set for a switch to Real Madrid, and Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams. But Barcola is now the firm favourite for a switch to Merseyside, with Liverpool having received encouragement ahead of an opening bid.

‌



According to The Telegraph, Barcola is unwilling to sign a new contract at the Parc des Princes, with his current deal set to expire in 2028. As a result, he is now prepared for the next stage of his career in the Premier League.

‌



Anfield officials have reportedly already held talks with the wideman’s representatives and it is said that the response has been favourable. That news has given Liverpool a considerable boost ahead of Andoni Iraola’s first season at the helm, particularly given the task that the Spaniard has in picking the club up after a disappointing campaign.

The task that Liverpool now have is convincing PSG to sell. The French club were previously keen to bank around £145m should they approve a move - having used Morgan Rogers’ £117m switch to Chelsea as a guide.

Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG READ MORE :

Liverpool forced to change pre-season plans as Reds hit with travel chaos READ MORE :

As it stands Liverpool are ready to lodge an opening offer in the region of around £110m but with PSG wanting considerably more than that, it remains to be seen if Anfield chiefs would be willing to break the British transfer record to sign him.

‌



Should talks progress positively, Barcola will then be offered at least a five-year deal to move to Anfield.

Barcola has been with PSG since a 2023 switch from French rivals Lyon. Since then, he has scored 39 goals in 152 games, 13 of which came last season. He is also a 28-time French international, having also netted on six occasions for his country.

Should he complete a move to Anfield, he would become the third addition of the summer window for Liverpool. Jeremy Jacquet agreed a move back in January from French side Rennes, while Victor Munoz was recruited from Osasuna earlier this summer.

‌



View 2 Images Liverpool have already been in touch with Barcola's representatives (Image: Getty Images)

Asked if he had a number in his mind of how many players he would want to sign last week, boss Iraola replied: “No, I think it’s difficult to say a number when the market is open, and you have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

“There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

Article continues below

“But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have. We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but is still not the ideal situation. So, it will depend on a lot of things.”

Sports.title: FIFA come down hard on Argentina stars as charges handed out after World Cup final brawl
Sports.content:
FIFA come down hard on Argentina stars as charges handed out after World Cup final brawl

FIFA have come down hard on three members of the Argentina side following the World Cup confrontation after full-time with Leandro Paredes among those charged

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes was hugely criticised for his actions after the World Cup final (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto, Getty Images)

FIFA have charged Argentina pair Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes following their roles in the unsavoury scenes that followed the World Cup final.

‌



Tensions boiled over at the MetLife Stadium in New York after the Spanish had claimed the second World Cup triumph courtesy of Ferran Torres' strike in extra-time. Argentina had been ill-tempered throughout and saw Enzo Fernandez sent-off in the final moments of regulation time.

‌



But the two teams were involved in a mass confrontations after the match, with Molina and Paredes singled out. FIFA have taken a look at the various incidents and come down with charges for the two men from Argentina.

‌



Molina has been hit by two FIFA charges for assault, one count being completed and one count being attempted, as well as one count of unsporting behaviour. Paredes, who was shown red after the final whistle before it was later rescinded, has to deal with with three counts of assault. Argentinian coach Ayala has been handed one count of assault and one count of unsportsmanlike behaviour.

FIFA open disciplinary proceedings after Argentina's Falklands banner vs England READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez reveals why Argentina turned backs on Spain players lifting World Cup READ MORE :

Ayala later apologised on Valencia Capital Radio: "Of course I'm sorry. Given my position, I cannot allow a feeling, or whatever I might receive from the other party, to affect my mood or my actions.

"For me, we need to draw a line and leave it at that. It was more of a shove than anything else, it wasn't a punch as they're making it out to be. It was a reaction to something he said, but that's it. If I see him, I'll obviously apologise to him in person."

‌



Spain midfielder Gavi is the only member of the victorious side to find himself in hot water as the Barcelona star was charged with one count of unsporting behaviour.

View 2 Images Argentina were accused of lacking class following the scenes at the MetLife Stadium (Image: Al Bello, Getty Images)

Argentina's conduct was widely condemned and Alan Shearer said on the BBC: "Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them. There is no place or space for that. We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Article continues below

FIFA have also opened up disciplinary proceedings against the Argentinian FA for their display of a Falklands-themed banner against England during the World Cup. After downing the Three Lions in the last four several players paraded a banner which read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta shares exciting transfer update as Arsenal chase Vinicius Jr - 'A lot is happening'
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta shares exciting transfer update as Arsenal chase Vinicius Jr - 'A lot is happening'

Arsenal are in the market for further new signings this summer, and Mikel Arteta has provided a transfer update days after the club's interest in Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr emerged

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has provided an Arsenal transfer update (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has teased that “a lot is happening” at Arsenal this summer as the club continues to work on its plans for the transfer window.

The Gunners have been linked with some big names of late, with Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr having emerged as a key target for the reigning Premier League champions.

Arsenal have expressed an interest in signing the Brazil international this summer, whose future at the Santiago Bernabeu is uncertain with no new contract agreed.

‌



Recent updates in the last 24 hours have claimed that Arsenal face a tough task to sign Vinicius, with the expectation that the 26-year-old will remain with the La Liga giants.

It has since been reported by football.london, though, that this is not necessarily the case. It is believed that a transfer to Arsenal remains very much on the table.

Sports.title: Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG
Sports.content:
Liverpool takeover plan clear as billionaires approached over buying stake from FSG

Amit Bhatia's investment group are reportedly in talks with Fenway Sports Group over a minority stake of up to 30 per cent in Liverpool FC

View 2 Images Liverpool owners FSG are in talks with an Amit Bhatia-led group over a minority investment. (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Amit Bhatia's consortium is reportedly eyeing a controlling stake in Liverpool as they remain in talks with owners Fenway Sports Group over a minority investment.

‌



According to Bloomberg, the son-in-law of steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal is aiming to acquire ownership of the Reds amid talks of a 30 per cent share.

‌



FSG confirmed last week that the British-Indian entrepreneur had approached Anfield figures as part of a consortium to obtain make a minority investment.

‌



Figures such as Amazon's Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin are said to have been approached to join forces to take over Liverpool.

Sky News revealed this week that Saverin, one of the architects behind the social media platform, has been sounded out to join the group of investors.

Crystal Palace work on transfers with Pierre Sage set to lose target to Premier League rival READ MORE :

Discussions are continuing over a substantial minority stake as part of Liverpool's search for additional investment into the football club following the arrangement with Dynasty Equity in 2023, which was valued between £82million and £164m.

‌



Liverpool are in the United States as part of their pre-season preparations ahead of Andoni Iraola's maiden campaign at Anfield.

Following their 4-2 victory against Sunderland, club legends Ian Rush and Robbie Fowler helped unveil the new away strip in New York City, ahead of their friendly clash with Wrexham (12.30am on Thursday).

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Chief executive Billy Hogan was speaking to Bloomberg and offered an update on the situation on Merseyside.

He said: "I can only refer back to the statement from FSG last week that we have been approached by a consortium that's led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia for a strategic minority investment in the club.

"And I wouldn't say anything other than that at this point."

‌



An FSG statement last week read: "An investment consortium led, managed and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

View 2 Images Jeff Bezos has been approached over investing in Liverpool (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

The Mittal family, Bhatia's in-laws, have an expanding portfolio of sports clubs. Lahkshmi's son, Aditya Mittal, pumped $1billion into becoming co-owner of NBA side Boston Celtics, while he fell short in a recent attempt to acquire American Football heavyweights Seattle Seahawks.

Article continues below

Indian Premier League powerhouses Rajasthan Royals saw a 75 per cent stake in the cricket franchise change hands for $1.65bn. The speculation surrounding a strategic investment arrives during a spell of upheaval at Liverpool, with Michael Edwards departing FSG as their CEO of football.

Sporting director Richard Hughes remains strongly linked with a move to Saudi Arabia to take charge of operations at Pro League giants Al-Hilal.

Sports.title: FIFA open disciplinary proceedings after Argentina's Falklands banner vs England
Sports.content:
FIFA open disciplinary proceedings after Argentina's Falklands banner vs England

Argentina stars controversially unfurled a Falklands-themed banner after their World Cup semi-final win against England and FIFA have now taken action

View 2 Images Argentina players parade a Falklands flag (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA have opened up disciplinary proceedings against the Argentinian FA for their display of a Falklands-themed banner against England during the World Cup.

‌



A number of players were seen parading the flag after their 2-1 win against England in Atlanta earlier this month. The banner read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates to 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

‌



Former Spurs player Giovani Lo Celso, as well as current star Cristian Romero, were seen celebrating with the banner, while the former then laid it on the floor in front of the Argentina fans. An investigation was launched by FIFA in the immediate aftermath

‌



And FIFA have now confirmed that they are taking disciplinary action for the display of the banner, as well as the behaviour of a host of the side's players throughout the tournament. A statement from FIFA accused Argentina of: "Using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discrimination and racist abuse, as well as order and security at matches in light of discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in several matches."

UEFA threatens World Cup boycott as FIFA governance crisis deepens over Infantino deadline READ MORE :

Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup READ MORE :

One of the other games that FIFA have been taking a close look at is the final itself. They have charged Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes for assault for their respective parts in a post-match brawl in New Jersey. The former has been charged with two counts, one completed and one attempted, while Paredes faces three counts.

Argentina coach Roberto Ayala is also facing one count. Molina and Thiago Almada are also facing additional FIFA charges of unsporting behaviour, alongside Spain midfielder Gavi.

‌



The charges come after a leaked letter from FIFA president Gianni Infantino was shared in which he congratulated Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia for the "professionalism" his side showed throughout the tournament.

View 2 Images Argentina celebrated wit the banner after defeating England (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

Argentina eventually lost the final 1-0 to Spain, Ferran Torres' extra time strike securing victory for Luis de la Fuente's men. They booked their spot in the final with a controversial semi-final win against England.

‌



Anthony Gordon had given the Three Lions the lead, only for goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez to turn the game on its head.

Controversy continues to surround FIFA and Infantino, having unveiled a plan to sell a share in the World Cup to foreign investors - a plot that has been met with serious opposition by UEFA, the FA and even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Sports.title: UEFA and Andy Burnham among those to hit back at FIFA's World Cup sale proposal
Sports.content:
UEFA and Andy Burnham among those to hit back at FIFA's World Cup sale proposal

FIFA's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup, a proposal ultimately led by Gianni Infantino, has received heavy backlash as leading figures and organisations hammer the concept

View 4 Images Gianni Infantino is looking to sell stakes in the World Cup (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

FIFA's plan, led by president Gianni Infantino, to sell off stakes in the World Cup has been met with near worldwide condemnation.

‌



It is the latest power grab from Infantino with the FIFA chief looking to offload aspects of its football competitions - with the World Cup being the biggest lure - to private investors via associates of US President Donald Trump.

‌



Fans, politicians and regional governing bodies have criticised the move, made by a man whose popularity throughout the game is at an all-time low following a World Cup that charged fans huge sums and overlooked rules of the game to put on a half-time show in the World Cup final.

‌



Infantino is trying to turn heads of the federations, whom support he needs, by claiming £15million of funding will be given to all Fifa countries to "develop the game" if and when the deal is finalised.

Ruthless Gianni Infantino's threat to FIFA members as he sets World Cup sale date READ MORE :

In a show of power, bordering on dictatorship, Infantino has claimed that anyone who is not on board with his proposal will receive less funding, effectively creating a two-tier system.

FIFA did not raise the landmark strategy during meetings with football associations in New York on the eve of the World Cup final, leading to surprise among those involved. Football's governing body would retain control of the enterprise, but offer minority stakes in it to private investors to raise up to $4.2bn.

‌



But the move has been smacked down by the likes of UEFA, Concacaf and Prime Minister Andy Burnham - whilst the FA have said they are "deeply concerned" but left scope to comment further when the time comes.

New PM hammers 'sell outs'

Burnham, the new Labour leader, has been looking to get the public onside in his opening weeks and claiming that football "belongs to the fans" is a good way to begin.

View 4 Images Andy Burnham has taken aim at FIFA's plan (Image: Kirsty Wigglesworth/Pool AP via)

‌



He wrote on X: "Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

"The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will."

FA hit out

The FA have taken a more measured approach, and admitted that they only have limited information on which to comment. They've by no means backed FIFA's plan but have said they will give greater comment when the proposal is fully transparent.

‌



An FA statement read: "We were completely unaware of this proposal and no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

View 4 Images England, who have continually been snubbed as World Cup hosts by FIFA, lost in the semi-finals earlier this month (Image: Julian Finney - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

"Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved. When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further."

‌



UEFA - FIFA divide grows

UEFA have taken as hard a stance as you possibly could. Relations between them have continued to worsen in recent years. UEFA are the strongest continental governing body and can boast gems like the Champions League. Their President Aleksander Ceferin refused to attend the World Cup final following a series of disagreements with Infantino over disciplinary procedures, refereeing logistics and match operations.

They said in a statement: "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously.

"So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game. The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

‌



View 4 Images UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin is known to be against a lot of FIFA's ideas (Image: Toya Sarno Jordan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

European nations are discussing boycotting the World Cup if Infantino pushes ahead with plans to sell off part of FIFA to private investors, according to Sky News.

CONACAF and AFC's strong statements

The governing body of North America and the Caribbean, CONCACAF, have ultimately just handed over their countries to that FIFA could host the biggest World Cup in history - but they've slammed the global organisation.

‌



“Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,” their statement read. “We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

The AFC, Asian football's governing body, echoed these concerns, saying: “The AFC was not consulted on the proposal and is disappointed that a matter of such significance entered the public domain before the AFC family had been afforded the opportunity to examine and discuss it through the appropriate and established governance channels.

Article continues below

“While the AFC recognises the importance of exploring innovative approaches that can strengthen the future of global football, initiatives of this scale and consequence must be founded upon the principles of good governance, transparency and meaningful consultation."

Sports.title: Crystal Palace work on transfers with Pierre Sage set to lose target to Premier League rival
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace work on transfers with Pierre Sage set to lose target to Premier League rival

New Crystal Palace head coach Pierre Sage has endured a tough pre-season to date as he prepares to welcome back the club's soaring World Cup stars

View 5 Images Pierre Sage has had a challenging start to life in the Crystal Palace hot-seat

Replacing Oliver Glasner was never going to be easy for Pierre Sage. But just 24 days out from Crystal Palace's Premier League opener at Everton, the 47-year-old Frenchman has already been exposed to the size of the task at hand.

The Eagles kickstarted pre-season with a bang, thrashing Swindon Town 5-1 before they were thumped 3-0 at nearby Bromley.

Palace lacked cutting edge and rather worryingly, looked defensively frail. Those bad habits also plagued their Como Cup Group A opener - a 45-minute exhibition - against Sage's former team, Lens, on Tuesday in Italy.

‌



The Conference League winners were hammered 3-0 and to rub salt into open wounds, ex-striker Odsonne Edouard struck a brace.

A goalless draw in their corresponding group fixture against Famalicao, though they eventually won the corresponding penalty shootout, means Palace will now participate in the fifth-place play-off on Friday evening. That is the least of their worries.

Brentford confirm Jordan Henderson exit as shock Chelsea transfer edges closer READ MORE :

Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made READ MORE :

While Sage's favoured 3-4-3 system is not too dissimilar from Oliver Glasner's highly-successful 3-4-2-1, he is trying to instill different principles, such as press triggers - something the players are still acclimatising too.

Within the club, there is thought to be a sense of calm, despite recent poor pre-season results.

Brazilian attacker Matheus Franca, back from his Vasco da Gama loan where he scored only once in 27 appearances, has been one of few positives in recent weeks.

View 5 Images Odsonne Edouard netted twice against his former club Crystal Palace in the Como Cup for Lens

‌



Brennan Johnson's struggles following his £35m January arrival have continued and transfer business has been slow thus far.

Chairman Steve Parish was Stateside for the latter stages of the World Cup and spent the evening of the final discussing the sale of Maxence Lacroix, poised to reach £52million, with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali in New York.

Financially, the Lacroix deal is further evidence of Palace's sharp recruitment work given he cost just £18m from Wolfsburg in 2024.

‌



He departs - no formal announcement has been made to date - as a full France international having also lifted three trophies (FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League) but replacing a player of his quality, after also losing captain Marc Guehi in January, will prove difficult.

View 5 Images Maxence Lacroix is set to join Chelsea from Crystal Palace (Image: Jared C. Tilton - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu - released by the Gunners last summer following a serious knee injury - is trialing at Palace with a view to earning a permanent contract. There have already been positive discussions on potential terms.

‌



The Japan international, who was also offered a three-year deal by Venezia while attracting interest from Sassuolo and Torino, can play in multiple roles across the backline but there are still some question marks over his fitness.

Augsburg centre-back Chrislain Matsima was a leading target and two formal bids were rejected but for now, negotiations are off as the German club shifted the goalposts.

View 5 Images Crystal Palace's negotiations for Augsburg defender Chrislain Matsima have gone cold

‌



Raphael Le Guen, a 19-year-old prospect from Brest, was in London for talks last week and personal terms have been agreed but the Eagles are yet to submit an offer as they ponder their options which also include Trabzonspor's 6ft 4in Nigerian centre-half Chibuike Nwaiwu.

Toulouse's Charlie Cresswell, Lens' Ismaelo Ganiou, who played against Palace on Tuesday, and Lecce's Tiago Gabriel have also been assessed and it's possible two new centre-backs arrive following the departure of veteran Nathaniel Clyne, confirmed earlier today.

The south Londoners were also open to re-exploring a move for Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez but he suffered a fractured metatarsal at the World Cup with Ecuador and could miss the start of the new season. It remains to be seen whether their interest could be revisited later in the window, depending on his recovery.

‌



Palace saw a sizeable bid, it would have been a Belgian record, rejected in the closing stages of the January window and his agents were at Selhurst Park for the Conference League semi-final win over Shakhtar Donetsk in May.

Keeping key stars will be just as important for Sage. Liverpool are among Adam Wharton's long-standing admirers but he's currently nursing an ankle injury and was left behind for the Como Cup.

Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare, who won the Coupe de France under Sage last season, had been identified as a potential replacement but Brentford are now on pole to clinch a deal that would be worth upwards of £41m providing there is no drastic U-turn.

‌



View 5 Images Mamadou Sangare won the Coupe de France under Pierre Sage at Lens

Palace have been weighing up a move as recently as the past 48 hours for the Mali international, who made the Ligue 1 Team of the Year last term but such a substantial investment would restrict spending power where other positions are concerned.

Sangare was rested in both Como Cup matches on Tuesday due to advanced negotiations with Brentford, who have now agreed the mutual termination of Jordan Henderson's contract.

‌



Manchester United also appreciate Ismaila Sarr while Chadi Riad's representatives have fielded loose enquiries over a return to La Liga. Neither are for sale.

Marauding wing-back Daniel Munoz is also thought to be open to a new challenge, should an appealing opportunity arise. He is attracting interest from the Saudi Pro League but remains a focal part of Palace's plans.

For Palace, this is a pre-season like no other as 10 of their players reached the World Cup knockout stages. Welcoming them back evidently cannot come soon enough.

Sports.title: Duckett stars as Rockets hand first defeat of season to Fire in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets handed Welsh Fire a first defeat of the season in The Hundred in a one-sided affair at Sophia Gardens.

The visitors chased down a below-par target of 123 with 28 balls to spare, Ben Duckett seeing the Rockets to victory with an unbeaten 52.

The start of the Rockets' chase was not fluent by any means but the Fire bowlers were sloppy, giving away four free-hits in the powerplay and seven in total.

Duckett faced the first four, only finding the boundary once, but he and Finn Allen (33) still managed to move the visitors onto 42-0 after 25 balls with little cause for concern.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Welsh Fire's Joe Root was bowled by Matt Henry after a failed attempt at a scoop shot in the match against Trent Rockets

The explosive Allen began to accelerate, taking 17 runs off Sam Cook's first five. He and Duckett cruised along against an uninspired Fire attack, taking the score to 75 before Allen fell lbw to fellow Kiwi Rachin Ravindra for 33.

Duckett, joined by Tom Banton (31), continued on his merry way, bringing up a second half-century in as many games, this time from 42 balls, as the Rockets made it two wins from three.

Hosts Fire had earlier ended their batting powerplay on 26-2, having been asked to bat first. They lost Phil Salt and Joe Root for five runs apiece to the seam of Matt Henry (2-16), the latter failing to connect with a ramp.

After reaching 59-2 at halfway, the Fire looked to push on, but proceeded to lose three wickets in the next 14 balls, including the set Matt Short for 36 from 26.

Jordan Cox (33) countered by launching Mitchell Santner's left-arm spin for three consecutive sixes, but perished going for a fourth, spectacularly caught on the cover boundary by a diving Allen.

Fire then limped to 122-7 with Asa Tribe (13no) and Chris Woakes (4no) failing to find the boundary off Mohammad Amir and Lewis Gregory in the closing stages of the innings.

Their target would prove easily surpassable by Trent Rockets, who moved up to second in the table with their second win from three games.

'The bowlers take credit for the win'

Image: Ben Duckett credited the bowling attack for the win (ECB Images)

Meerkat Match Hero - Ben Duckett - on Sky Sports Cricket:

"The bowlers were superb. Coming here, we spoke about adapting to the pitch as early as you can. They take massive credit for this win.

"My aim was to try and get through the powerplay and then it might actually become easier. It's made a lot easier when you've got Finn Allen at the other end whacking it.

"Four free-hits really help as well, but, to be honest, I really struggled to find rhythm throughout that whole innings. I'm pretty sure everyone saw that. Finn played beautifully and Bants came in and took all the pressure off me.

What's next in The Hundred?

Sports.title: Player at centre of viral 'Clicky Ponting' scandal suspended
Sports.content:
The cricketer at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating allegations has been suspended and will not play again "for the foreseeable future", the club have announced.

Saltburn Cricket Club is under investigation by the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League amid cheating accusations against one of their players.

Saltburn, who have made national headlines, were due to face Marton Cricket Club on Wednesday but have conceded the contest.

It comes after footage of an alleged finger-clicking incident, which took place in a Division Two match between Saltburn and Norton Cricket Club on Saturday, went viral on social media.

The clip has over 7.5m views and the scandal has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting', after the former Australia captain, Ricky Ponting.

Some users have suggested the fielder, seen standing at slip, clicks his fingers as the ball passes an opponent's bat to imitate the noise of an edge.

The clip shows Saltburn's wicketkeeper then catching the ball behind the stumps. The team appeals to the umpire, who gives the batter out.

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League says it has launched an investigation into the matter.

A statement released on Saltburn's social media channels read: "This is issued in response to the widely publicised complaint made against a Saltburn Cricket Club member and, as a consequence, against the club more generally.

"We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric club, we are fully cooperating with the NYS League's investigation.

"We believe that the club acted decisively as soon as the complaint and investigation were made known to us. The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation."

The player in question, when contacted by the Daily Mail, said: "Naturally, I cannot comment on that. I also cannot answer any questions because I am currently at work."

"The League have received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday," a statement from North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League said.

"A full investigation has been initiated, and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made."

Saltburn currently sit top of the Division Two league table having won 10 of their 15 matches this season.

The team's wicketkeeper also leads the league for the most fielding dismissals - 34, of which 31 came from catches behind the stumps.

Earlier in July, Saltburn secured a 22-run victory against Shildon Railway Cricket Club, a match in which their wicketkeeper took eight catches. No Test wicketkeeper has taken more than seven catches in an innings.

After the video surfaced on social media, Middlesbrough second XI captain Rory Cotterill alleged that two further incidents had taken place during a game between his side and Saltburn in June.

Banton: 'Clicky Ponting' kind of clever but not acceptable

The story has engulfed the cricketing world, with discussions raging about what the next steps will be.

For England and Somerset's Tom Banton, while it is a "clever" way of cricket it is not one that can be justified.

"It's interesting, kind of clever in a way. But I cannot vouch for things like that, it's not acceptable," he told Sky Sports.

"It's been caught out and something is going to be done about it because I'm not sure it's in the rules of cricket."
