1.50 Coral Kincsem Heritage Handicap: CIARRAI ABU , who arrives with a progressive profile and some local knowledge, is primed to go well.

‌



On the back of a debut sixth at the Curragh last August, the gelded son of Study Of Man moved to Harry Eustace, running second in a Brighton maiden in October before returning to land a maiden over this afternoon’s course and distance at the beginning of May.

‌



Eustace was keen to give my selection further match practice around the South Downs and Ciarrai Abu started life in the handicap sphere over Goodwood’s mile on his next outing.

‌



Sent off the 5-2 favourite for a 10-runner event for three-year-olds, he was momentarily tightened for room running to the furlong pole before running on strongly to take fourth, beaten a nose, half a length and a neck, behind Annastarzy.

Ciarrai Abu, whose name translates from Irish Gaelic as ’Up Kerry’, was back to winning form 20 days ago when nailing Crest Of Fire on the line under Kaiya Fraser, who makes way for George Wood today.

His finishing efforts over a mile suggest Ciarrai Abu will improve again over an additional two furlongs, and a 6lb rise looks within range for a three-year-old who retains a significant ‘up’ side. Savvy Disko is on a hat-trick and commands respect, along with Decade Of Time and Birgham Dub .

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 CIARRAI ABU, 2 SAVVY DISKO, 3 BIRGHAM DUB

View 7 Images Simon Crisford: trains Newsboy's pick with son Ed

2.25 Markel Richmond Stakes: FLANN SUNNA has won both his starts with ease and is ready for this step up to Group 2 company for the stable that captured this race with Vandeek three years ago.

‌



The son of Blue Point - dam Lady Princess was a won twice in Ireland as a two-year-old, including at Listed level - went under the hammer for 200,000 guineas as a yearling last October before being put into training with Simon and Ed Crisford.

Sent off at 7-2 in a field of 13 when making his racecourse debut at Windsor last month, Flann Sunna got his career off to the perfect start, sprinting clear of his rivals to beat next-time-out scorer Perfect Nation by three and a half lengths.

My selection went to Ascot 18 days later for a seven-runner conditions event, again over six furlongs, and put up an impressive performance under Jack Mitchell - William Buick is at the controls this afternoon - tanking into the lead on the run to the two-furlong pole and careering away to humble Mysterious Times by four and three-quarter lengths.

‌



The evidence of his first two races is that Flann Sunna hasn’t scratched far beneath the surface and, with a truckload of as-yet untapped potential to draw upon, he’s expected to remain unbeaten. Cut A Dash and Night In Vegas, a close-up fourth and fifth in Royal Ascot’s Coventry Stakes, hold obvious podium claims, while Big Cigar is another to throw into the mix.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 FLANN SUNNA, 2 CUT A DASH, 3 BIG CIGAR

View 7 Images Trainer Joseph O'Brien saddles Newsboy's tip (Image: Getty Images)

‌



3.00 Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes: ENCELADUS needs to improve if he is to make the transition from handicap to Group 3 level - but he’s taken to do exactly that.

With an official rating of 99, the Joseph O’Brien-saddled son of Sea The Stars is currently a few pounds shy of rivals Venetian Lace (110), Bay Of Brilliance and Geryon (both 107). But the evidence of his two starts this term is that Dylan Browne McMonagle’s partner is very much on an upward curve and poised to produce another personal best today.

Third in maidens at the Curragh and Naas as a two-year-old last autumn, my selection returned from 195 days off to lift a similar event at Cork in April by a head from Almazann. O’Brien gave Enceladus his handicap debut in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot, for which he went off at 7-1 in a field of 19.

‌



And he progressed past his opening mark of 89, running to a half-length margin from Al Azd, who polished the form with a runaway success at the royal racecourse last Friday. It will be a shock if Enceladus doesn’t have plenty more to give on the fifth outing of his life, and the hat-trick is on the cards.

Bay Of Brilliance, Shaihaan and Venetian Lace are taken to fight it out for the minor medals.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ENCELADUS, 2 BAY OF BRILLIANCE, 3 SHAIHAAN

‌



View 7 Images Ryan Moore returns to the winners' circle on Diamond Necklace (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

3.35 Qatar Nassau Stakes: DIAMOND NECKLACE is impossible to get away from as she bids for a sixth win from as many starts, and a fourth consecutive Group 1 triumph.

Aidan O’Brien is never short of talent in the two-year-old department but, even by Ballydoyle’s standards, 2025 was a good year, especially with Precise, True Love and Diamond Necklace flying the flag for the fillies.

‌



Each of the trio managed to score at the highest level, with Diamond Necklace putting into the Group 1 pot with a one-length call in the Prix Marcel Boussac at Longchamp on the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe undercard in October, on the back of wins at the Curragh and Leopardstown.

The daughter of St Mark’s Basilica returned to Paris for France’s version of the 1,000 Guineas, the Poule d’Essai des Pouliches, in May and justified favouritism in style, bursting clear inside the final furlong to humble The Last Dance by three lengths.

Diamond Necklace had to work a good bit harder when taking on 10 opponents for the Prix de Diane over an extended mile and a quarter at Chantilly last time out but extended her winning run to five with a short-neck margin from Pink Panthera.

‌



That success proved that Ryan Moore’s mount can operate not only at this afternoon’s trip but also on fast ground, and it will be a shock if her colours are lowered for the first time. See The Fire, twice placed in this race, is the choice to chase the market leader home, ahead of Bogotaz and Friendly Soul.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 DIAMOND NECKLACE, 2 SEE THE FIRE, 3 BOGOTAZ

Don't miss out! Pick up your paper from Tuesday July 28 until Saturday August 1, 2026.

‌



4.10 Buccellati Handicap: NAANA’S SHADOW, beaten when upped to Listed level at York last time, still has more to offer on her return to the handicap scene.

The daughter of Havana Grey, a one-time winner for Alice Haynes as a juvenile last year, joined Katie Scott during the winter and has gone from strength to strength in the Galashiels-based trainer’s care.

Having needed her first run for the thick end of six months at Southwell in April, Naana’s Shadow scored at Catterick Bridge next time before a close third at York’s May fixture.

‌



My selection was back in business in the 3YO “Dash” Handicap on the Oaks undercard next time and made it three wins from her last four attempts when beating Shrodinger’s Cat by a short head back on the Knavesmire at the end of last month.

A 16-1 shot for York’s Listed City Walls Stakes 19 days ago, Naana’s Shadow finished ninth of 13, just over three lengths behind winner Redorange.

It’s inconvenient that the handicapper raised her 3lb to a new British Horseracing Authority rating of 94 on the strength of that run, but Naana’s Shadow is far from done with and Goodwood promises to suit.

‌



In an open contest for three-year-olds, Shrodinger’s Cat, Shes Got A Brother, Noble View and One And Gone all have a role to play.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 NAANA’S SHADOW, 2 NOBLE VIEW, 3 ONE AND GONE

View 7 Images Richard Hughes: trains Newsboy pick (Image: Getty Images)

‌



4.45 Whispering Angel Nursery Handicap: THE BOOKKEEPER returns to seven furlongs on his nursery debut and is the selection to look after the bottom line.

Plenty went wrong when Richard Hughes gave the Sioux Nation-sired youngster his racecourse bow over five furlongs at Salisbury in mid-May, but The Bookkeeper still showed plenty of promise for the future with a running-on fifth behind subsequent Norfolk Stakes hero Orthodox.

An additional quarter mile triggered a step forward when my selection took on three rivals for a novice stakes at Haydock Park eight days later and beat Pat’s Cash by three-quarters of a length. Splitting the difference at six furlongs for the Woodcote Conditions Stakes on Epsom’s Oaks undercard last time out, The Bookkeeper then ran to a similar level of form, coming home with purpose to take fourth behind Hickory Lad.

‌



That race has worked out well, with third Rlasthope and sixth home Ardad Steve winning next time, and The Bookkeeper will be well served by going back up in distance. Hughes’s eyes no doubt lit up when he learned a kind draw in stall two and his securing of Ryan

Moore to do the steering aboard this promising juvenile is the icing on the cake. Dangers lurk at every corner, with Everatease, The Ginger Kid and Caeruleus at the top of a long shortlist.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 THE BOOKKEEPER, 2 EVERATEASE, 3 THE GINGER KID

‌



View 7 Images Aidan O'Brien: trains Newsboy tip (Image: Megan Ridgwell/The Jockey Club)

5.20 Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes: SO LOVELY rates a worthy favourite to get off the mark at the second time of asking.

Even at this most prestigious meeting, few horses will boast a more illustrious pedigree than the Aidan O’Brien-trained filly, a daughter of the Coolmore Stud’s late and lamented Wootton Bassett and Love, whose five Group 1 successes included victory in the 1,000 Guineas and Oaks six years ago.

‌



So Lovely’s career journey began at Leopardstown two weeks ago, when she locked horns with five opponents for a one-mile fillies’ maiden.

Bellesque, representing O’Brien’s son Joseph, went off the even-money favourite and duly justified her position at the head of the betting. But there was a good deal to like about So Lovely’s introduction.

Racing at the back of the pack under Wayne Lordan - Ryan Moore steps in for the mount this afternoon - the Ballydoyle two-year-old made ground towards the principals once in line for home and ran on under a hand ride to get within three parts of a length of the winner.

‌



The step back to seven furlongs shouldn’t be an issue and So Lovely should deliver on that debut promise. York runner-up Elevating and debutantes Beguiled and La Torre are also among those who make appeal.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 SO LOVELY, 2 ELEVATING, 3 LA TORRE

View 7 Images David Menuisier: trainer of Get Outta Here (Image: PA)

‌



5.55 HKJC World Pool Handicap: GET OUTTA HERE should not be dismissed after claiming gold, silver and bronze on his first three starts in handicaps.

Having qualified for a British Horseracing Authority mark of 70, the son of Zelzal and Jamie Spencer beat five rivals at Lingfield Park at the end of May.

Get Outta Here came within a nose of the follow-up over this course and distance 20 days later, galloping on strongly to the line after being made to wait for a gap but just coming off the worse of a photo-finish with Annastarzy.

‌



Sent off the 13-8 favourite to gain compensation at York last time out, the David Menuisier trainee came home in third behind Illy’s Roo. The result doesn’t tell the whole story, however, as Get Outta Here attempted to make inroads on the leaders just as the race was hotting up before that effort took its toll close home.

From an unchanged rating of 79, and with hold-up king Spencer back on board, Get Outta Here is taken to go well once more. Exclusive Code is feared most, ahead of Euston Hall and Wild Thoughts.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 GET OUTTA HERE, 2 EXCLUSIVE CODE, 3 EUSTON HALL

Sports.title: Billy Loughnane dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulates Frankel
Sports.content:
Billy Loughnane dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulates Frankel

The 20-year-old was compared to Spain's World Cup winner after passing the sternest examination of his big race credentials in the £1.5 million Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes at Goodwood

View 3 Images Billy Loughnane has been compared to Lamine Yamal (Image: Getty Images)

Billy Loughnane was dubbed ‘racing’s Lamine Yamal’ after Bow Echo emulated the legendary Frankel at Goodwood on Wednesday.

The £1.5 million Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes is Britain’s top mile race, the first contest in which the top three-year-olds take on the best older milers.

The George Boughey-trained Bow Echo came to Goodwood with unbeaten record having landed the 2,000 Guineas in May and St James’s Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot, both times beating Aidan O’Brien’s Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Gstaad. Just a short head had separated the pair at Ascot and the pair’s third clash threatened to be equally close.

It was never going to be as straightforward as Bow Echo’s 10-11 odds might have suggested with O’Brien running three horses in the 12 runner race.

Ryan Moore on Gstaad, whose stablemate Puerto Rico was outside him, had Loughnane in a pocket with two furlongs to run, leaving the favourite having to wait for his run.

For a moment it looked like Moore had stolen the race as he was able to get first run on his opponent to hit the front half a furlong out, but Loughnane angled his horse to the outside and Bow Echo ran down Gstaad to score by half a length, triggering wild celebrations.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Three Group 1s in a row Billy Loughnane and Bow Echo (Image: Getty Images)

Bow Echo became the first horse since Frankel in 2011 to complete the 2,000 Guineas-St James’s Palace-Sussex hat-trick.

Top jockey turned trainer Johnny Murtagh pulled off the same hat-trick on Henrythenavigator when he was stable jockey to Aidan O’Brien.

Working as a pundit for ITV, he said: “Last week at the World Cup you had Lamine Yamal. Everyone was raving about him, 19, what he’s doing.

View 3 Images Billy Loughnane with Bow Echo's trainer George Boughey (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

“This is racing’s Lamine Yamal. He’s a special talent, he’s 20. The more big races he rides and wins like this, the more confident he’ll get.

“He’s got that little bit of confidence-cheeky about him, but he has to back it up and today, Bow Echo and himself did.”

Bow Echo’s programme could take him to France next for the Prix Jacques Le Marois or Prix du Moulin with the Breeders’ Cup Mile on the cards at the end of the year.

Loughnane said: “What a superstar horse. I say it every time I know how lucky I am to be able to ride a horse like this. I just feel so privileged.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

“They made life difficult for him but I always wanted to follow Ryan. I knew the pace would be on with the set up of the race. That plays into this horse’s strengths.

“I was boxed in between Ryan and Christophe, and I just had to wait to get out but once I did he just proved how good he is.

Article continues below

“Me and George watched plenty of Sussexes back and they always get on top of them late and get going early. It just keeps getting better.”

Sports.content:

Day three features more quality racing from the Glorious Goodwood meeting and our ace has found four selections from Thursday's card

View Image Steve Jones with his picks for Glorious Goodwood on ITV

‌



Named after a particularly good salmon fishing spot on the River Tweed, he won his only race as a two-year-old last year and he kicked off this season with a smooth victory on Southwell’s all-weather track.

‌



The form of that race worked out really well and, although it was over 1m4f, he hasn’t been getting home in better races over the same distance. He travelled into the straight as strongly as any of his rivals in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot but just couldn’t sustain his run.

The drop to 1m2f for the first time could do the trick. Have 1pt each-way at 14-1. Most bookies are paying out on four places.

He has loads of speed and drops to 5f for the first time. The last seven winners of this race had previously run over 6f and he is another. Have 1pt each-way at 9-1. Most firms are offering five places.

Sports.title: Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup
Sports.content:
Premier League wades into FIFA row after Gianni Infantino's threat to sell World Cup

With Gianni Infantino plotting to turn the World Cup into a business where shares can be bought and sold, the Premier League have issued their response

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's idea with the World Cup has evoked plenty of ire (Image: 2026 Alex Livesey - Danehouse)

The Premier League has publicly objected to Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors. He unveiled plans to launch a company called 'FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) which would bring the sale of FIFA's commercial rights together.

‌



After going through his idea, the Premier League issued a statement backing the position laid out by the European Leagues, which firmly expressed its opposition to Infantino's plan. The top flight of English football wrote: "The Premier League is a founder member of the European Leagues and fully supports this statement."

‌



The European Leagues issued a statement which read: "FIFA’s announcement that its President is pursuing private investment options for a new subsidiary, consolidating its commercial and event-related operations, represents a reckless and divisive development for world football. The World Cup should not be for sale.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"It is not FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal. Football’s success has always been built on a pyramidal open structure and the delicate balance between domestic and international football. Commercial opportunities must support these foundations, not risk altering them.

"This opaque process and unilateral proposal are part of a long-term pattern in FIFA’s decision-making – a pattern which prompted the European Leagues to lodge a complaint with the European Commission on the basis that FIFA’s imposition of decisions on the international match calendar constitutes an abuse of dominant position that violates European competition law.

‌



"Proposals relating to calendar and competitions, should be developed through transparent, accountable and inclusive processes, with meaningful engagement and consent from all stakeholders whose interests are affected, as explicitly requested by the Court of Justice of the EU in its 2023 Super League ruling.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"We have held productive meetings with the European Commission about this matter and have confidence that the legal decisions they take will continue to be in the best interests of fans and football communities.

‌



"European Leagues will continue to work with UEFA to safeguard the long-term interests of the game. We have faith that Federations/National Associations around the world will do the same as they scrutinise this proposal from the FIFA President."

It's understood Infantino has informed all of FIFA's 211 member associations they must agree to his World Cup sell-off plan by September 19 if they want the funding, which is believed to be around £30m for the 2027-30 FIFA cycle, which will also include a one-off windfall of £15m in January next year.

View 2 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino watched South Korea take on Czech Republic at the Guadalajara Stadium in Zapopan (Image: (Ulises RUIZ / AFP via Getty Images))

‌



UEFA president Alexander Ceferin is expected to amass the European governing body's 55 member nations, amid calls for a mass boycott of FIFA in response to the plan.

However, Czechian Football Association president David Trunda has already offered his support for Infantino's plan.

He said: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with Gianni Infantino and his team. Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

Article continues below

The proposal has received huge backing from Thrive Capital, who are part owned by Joshua Kusher whose brother Jared is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump.

Sports.title: Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna
Sports.content:
Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna

Michael Schumacher's health still remains a mystery with his wife Corinna keeping the F1 icon's recovery a private secret few people kz

View 3 Images Michael Schumacher has not been seen in public for over a decade (Image: Lars Baron, Bongarts/Getty Images)

Ex-racing driver Christian Danner has claimed there are rumours that Michael Schumacher is now in Majorca - but the F1 great's wife, Corinna, will not clarify if this is the case.

‌



Thirteen years have passed since the F1 great hit his head on a rock as a result of an horrific skiing accident. The seven-time World Drivers Championship winner has not been seen in public since he fell into a coma after the crash, with Corinna ensuring his recovery is kept an absolute secret.

‌



Danner has claimed he has heard Schumacher is living in an estate in Majorca while he continues his recovery, but insisted Corinna has kept any details tightly guarded. In January last year, it was claimed by the Daily Mail that the German is capable of sitting up after years of physical therapy, but is still unable to walk.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

In a recent interview with OLBG, Danner said: "There are all these rumours he's in Majorca, and they've put him in an estate there, and so forth. When I'm speaking to Corinna, she's not mentioning it. When I'm speaking to other people who could know, they don't tell me."

Corinna set out her position regarding Schumacher's recovery clearly, when she said: "We’re together. We live together at home. We do therapy.

‌



"We do everything we can to make Michael better and to make sure he’s comfortable. And to simply make him feel our family, our bond. Private is private’, as he always said.

View 3 Images Schumacher had his skiing accident 13 years ago (Image: JEAN-LOUP GAUTREAU, AFP via Getty Images)

"It’s very important to me that he can continue to enjoy his private life as much as possible. Michael always protected us and now we are protecting Michael.”

‌



In addition, Danner insisted the fact Schumacher still has not been seen in public suggests he is a long way from recovering. The close friend of the ex-Ferrari ace said: “However Michael looks, or under whatever conditions he's alive – I don't know – I want to see him again.

"The fact that he's not appearing anywhere indicates that he's probably not very well. But Formula 1's prepared for that. Formula 1's prepared for everything.

View 3 Images Corinna Schumacher has been determined to keep her husband's recovery secret (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media, Getty Images)

‌



"He's one of the heroes in the history of Formula 1, so if he would be happy and fit enough to come back, no matter the circumstances, in whatever condition, I think Formula 1 can cope with it easily."

He also added: "There are heroes in any kind of sport that have had a problem and have kind of fallen. But once they're alive, I think it does everyone a lot of good (to see them again).

"For me personally, it would be absolutely smashing to see him. I think that feeling is around for virtually everybody in Formula 1."

Sports.title: Ruthless Gianni Infantino's threat to FIFA members as he sets World Cup sale date
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has told FIFA’s 211 member associations to sign up to his World Cup sell-off plans by mid-September - or say goodbye to the prospect of almost $7.5billion in extra funding.

The plotting FIFA president has sent a letter to the associations, saying: “Should you wish to proceed, this $10billion package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together. Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme (development money) of $2.7billion as previously presented.”

Infantino has given members until September 19 to accept his proposal which, he promises, will see them get $40million for the 2027-30 FIFA cycle, starting with a one-off windfall of $20million in January, 2027.

Infantino knows that a lot of the associations will be tempted by the extra cash but his letter has produced a furious response from UEFA.

‌



UEFA issue new statement as Gianni Infantino sends threat over World Cup plan READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In its latest statement, UEFA said: “We have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan

“But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends.”

Aleksander Ceferin, the UEFA president, will today chair a meeting of its 55 member nations amidst growing calls for a European boycott of the World Cup and Club World Cup if Infantino’s scheme gets the go-ahead.

‌



But UEFA unity is far from guaranteed, with the president of the Czech Republic’s football association, David Trunda, already saying: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with Gianni Infantino and his team.

“Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

Trunda’s praise of the scheme - which would see a private company with links to the extended family of Donald Trump run FIFA competitions - is against most opinions voiced so far. But the Football Association were typically guarded in their mildly critical response.

‌



A statement read: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached. Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

The Welsh response was even more non-committal, with a FAW statement saying: “The Football Association of Wales has not yet received any substantial details from FIFA concerning the reported proposals.

“Consequently, the FAW is concerned that such matters have become public prior to being shared with FIFA’s Member Associations. We await receipt of FIFA’s full proposal before commenting further on this matter.”

‌



Despite a huge backlash, led in England by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, sources close to Infantino say he is hell-bent on getting the scheme voted through.

And now it remains to be seen if UEFA follow up their tough words with equally tough action.

Sports.title: England must boycott the Women's World Cup to stop Gianni Infantino selling football's soul
Sports.content:
Just when you thought Gianni Infantino had finally exhausted the depths of administrative sleaze, FIFA's supreme leader has managed to discover a brand new basement underneath the trapdoor.

For a decade now, the world's most preening, Teflon-coated football bureaucrat has glided through global corridors of power like a smoothly oiled Bond villain - a man whose moral compass spins so wildly it could unclog a backed-up sewer pipe... and it's little wonder, given nobody on earth is quite so proficient at unleashing fresh torrents of corporate cr*p upon the world.

We've watched him turn world football into a travelling circus of shameless sycophancy and endless cash-grabs. But his latest stunt isn't just another piece of administrative vandalism. It's an outright heist on the very soul of the game.

Infantino's latest brainwave is as brazen as it is grotesque: he wants to carve off FIFA's commercial rights - broadcasting, ticketing, licensing, the lot - and sell a 20 per cent stake in a new entity, FIFA Forward Enterprise, to private equity investors for $4.2billion (£3.16bn).

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

UEFA handed blow as Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup plan backed READ MORE :

And who, pray tell, is leading this financial feeding frenzy? An investment group fronted by Joshua Kushner - brother of Jared Kushner, Donald Trump's son-in-law. You genuinely couldn't write a script this eye-rollingly absurd.

This, lest we forget, comes right on the heels of the 2026 World Cup, where Infantino spent two months performing a series of breathtaking contortions to stay in President Trump's good books. We saw the ultimate humiliation when Trump personally phoned Infantino to complain about a red card shown to USA striker Folarin Balogun; lo and behold, FIFA's "independent" judicial committee magically suspended the ban.

Now, having allowed Trump to rewrite the rulebook on the fly, Infantino is handing the keys to the commercial treasury over to the President's extended family network. And to ensure nobody asks too many awkward questions, Infantino is dangling a £30million cash bribe in front of every national association, telling them to sign off on the sell-off by September 19 or risk losing their grassroots funding. It's classic mob-style governance: accept the envelope of cash, keep your mouth shut, and let the suit-and-tie vultures pick the bones clean.

‌



So, how has our very own Football Association responded to this existential assault on the game? On cue, Wembley's blazer-clad technocrats duly gathered in a softly lit boardroom, wrung their hands, and issued a statement expressing "deep concern." It's the administrative equivalent of throwing a soggy tissue at a roaring fire. Next up, perhaps they'll design a nice, polite lapel badge or a colourful warm-up top to really show how much they disapprove.

View 3 Images The way Infantino has cosied up to Donald Trump encapsulates the rot inside FIFA (Image: Getty Images)

We've seen this limp, hand-wringing film before. In Qatar, it was a brief, panicked flutter over rainbow armbands that vanished the second a yellow card was mentioned. In North America, it was polite, muted murmurs while Infantino effectively turned the World Cup draw into a political rally. The FA's idea of taking a stand usually has all the backbone of a jellyfish. They make polite noises in Zurich committee rooms, take their allocated seats in the VIP boxes, and watch quietly as Infantino counts his billfolds.

Enough. No more virtue-signalling. No more sternly worded press releases that Infantino uses to line his shredder. If Mark Bullingham and the FA genuinely care about protecting football from being auctioned off to private equity speculators and political cronies, they must reach for the nuclear button: England must threaten an immediate, total boycott of the 2027 Women's World Cup.

‌



And they shouldn't do it alone. They must immediately form an impenetrable European front alongside UEFA allies - Germany, France, Spain, the Netherlands - and deliver a blunt, non-negotiable ultimatum. Either Infantino withdraws the FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme permanently and bans private equity from owning commercial stakes in international tournaments, or he can watch the 2027 tournament implode without a single European team stepping onto the pitch.

Without the Lionesses, without defending champions Spain, and without the rest of Europe's elite, Infantino's shiny $20bn pitch to Wall Street collapses overnight. Private equity sharks do not invest billions in empty stadiums, depleted TV ratings, and second-rate substitute teams. Cut off the star power, and the money-men will scatter back into the shadows faster than you can say "conflict of interest."

View 3 Images The FA must boycott the Women's World Cup next year (Image: Getty Images)

We know this strategy works because we've seen the terrifying magic of righteous football fury before. Cast your mind back to the European Super League heist in 2021: a cartel of greedy billionaires attempting to ring-fence the sport, only to be completely obliterated within 48 hours by a tidal wave of fan power.

‌



When supporters took to the streets, blocked team buses, and made the ground shake beneath the owners' feet, those ruthless corporate conquerors folded like cheap deckchairs. If the FA's suits lack the spine to lead the charge against Infantino's privatised empire, then the fans must force their hand and light the touch paper once more.

For too long, football's spineless custodians have treated Gianni Infantino like bad weather - an unpleasant, unavoidable tax on existence to be endured under a squeaking umbrella while he quietly auctions off the family silver.

Well, the World Cup is not a sovereign kingdom, Infantino is not its feudal lord, and the global game does not belong to Wall Street suit-wearers or Florida golf club courtiers. It belongs to the terraces, the muddy park pitches, and the millions around the world who pour their lives into it.

The line in the sand is drawn, the fuse is lit, and the time for polite diplomatic bowing is over. The FA must finally grow a spine, grab the sledgehammer, and smash this corrupt racket to splinters before there is nothing left to save.

‌

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
