World.title: ¿Cuántas hectáreas han ardido? El mapa de los incendios activos más graves
World.content:
Desde el comienzo del año se han iniciado en España {{fires_year}} incendios que han quemado {{area_ha_year}} hectáreas, un {{es_area_over_mean}}% {{es_area_over_mean_relation}} más que la media de la última década, según los datos provisionales del Sistema de información europeo de incendios forestales (EFFIS) que miden la extensión de los fuegos a partir de imágenes satelitales. {{bigfires_year}} de estos fuegos han sido grandes incendios (de más de 500 hectáreas).

En el siguiente mapa mostramos dos cosas: los polígonos que actualiza EFFIS y otros estimados por EL PAÍS a partir de los puntos de calor que detectan los satélites. Usamos estos puntos para clasificar los incendios: cuando hay puntos de las últimas 24 horas sobre un incendio o sus inmediaciones se ven en rojo ( activo 24 horas ); cuando son de las últimas 48, pasan a naranja ( 48 horas ). Así, un incendio con polígono rojo y muchos puntos rojos será activo y reciente.

Cargando En el mapa se muestran los incendios activos consultados el --:-- y los puntos de calor 24 h 48 h, recogidos por distintos satélites hasta el --:--. Más incendios graves Desde mayo Cargando incendios activos...

La información de puntos de calor activos la recopilan cinco satélites de la NASA que detectan focos de temperaturas anómalas mediante sensores térmicos. Para determinar el perímetro del incendio usamos los datos del programa europeo EFFIS, basado en fotografías satelitales: mide el área quemada casi tiempo real, por lo que ofrece cifras provisionales y sirve para seguir la temporada al día. Sus números suelen ser algo más altos que los del Ministerio de Transición Ecológica, que ofrece la estadística oficial más precisa a partir de los partes de incendio de las comunidades autónomas, pero con semanas o meses de retraso. Ambos deben tomarse como una estimación que se consolidará al final de la temporada.

En el mapa también puede consultar las zonas de riesgo de incendios en el territorio. Este {{date_aemet}} habría peligro extremo de incendio en {{area_riesgo_extremo}}% de la superficie peninsular, según las estimaciones de Aemet.

¿Cómo está siendo la temporada?

Según los últimos datos actualizados de EFFIS, en España se han quemado {{area_ha_year}} hectáreas desde el principio de año hasta este {{today}}, por encima de la media de los últimos 20 años a estas altura de la temporada.

Ha despuntado también el número de incendios, que se sitúa ya en {{fires_year}} –sobre la media de {{fires_mean}}–, con un incremento del {{fires_summer_inc}}% desde el inicio del verano.

¿Qué está pasando en Europa?

En el conjunto de la Unión Europea, la superficie quemada asciende a {{ue_area_year}} hectareas, {{ue_aera_over_mean}} por encima de la media.

World.title: ¿Dónde hay alertas por calor? Consulte en qué municipios hay riesgo para la salud
World.content:
Compruebe en este mapa si se alcanzan niveles peligrosos hoy, mañana o pasado. Los avisos se basan en los umbrales establecidos por Sanidad y Aemet

[[dia]] [[verbo_dia]] [[alto_riesgo_muni]] municipios en zonas con riesgo alto para la salud por calor ([[perc_riesgo_alto_muni]]%), [[riesgo_medio_muni]] en riesgo medio ([[perc_riesgo_medio_muni]]%) y [[bajo_riesgo_muni]] en riesgo bajo ([[perc_bajo_riesgo_muni]]%). Puede consultar los datos para hoy, mañana y pasado en el siguiente mapa elaborado de forma automática a partir de los datos que el Ministerio de Sanidad y Aemet han publicado este miércoles.

🌡 🌡 🌡 Cargando

Qué es un nivel de alerta

El sistema de alertas sanitarias divide España en 182 zonas de meteosalud (las “regiones” que se ven el mapa) en los que se fijan umbrales de temperaturas máximas para cada una de ellas, basados en el aumento de la mortalidad en cada área cuando se supera un nivel de calor extremo.

Para determinar en cuál de los tres niveles de alerta se encuentra cada zona se tiene en cuenta cómo afectará el calor durante una ventana de 72 horas, dado el impacto sobre la salud del calor persistente. [[dia]], por ejemplo, [[verbo_dia]] [[alto_riesgo_zonas]] zonas de meteosalud en nivel 3 (el más alto) y [[riesgo_medio_zonas]] en nivel 2 en España.

En la siguiente tabla puede consultar las temperaturas previstas por la Aemet (Agencia Estatal de Meteorología) para los próximos días en los municipios de más de 50.000 habitantes y si se prevé que se supere el umbral de riesgo del área de meteosalud donde se encuentran.

AEMET mantiene avisos por altas temperaturas en [[comunidades_aemet]]

El otro sistema: Meteoalerta

Además de las alertas sanitarias, la Aemet cuenta con el plan Meteoalerta con el que la agencia activa sus avisos vinculados a las altas temperaturas. El siguiente mapa muestra las zonas que tienen avisos activos por temperaturas máximas.

Estos avisos se establecen de acuerdo con umbrales específicos para cada zona en un día concreto, sin el marco temporal de tres días que emplea el mapa del Ministerio de Sanidad y sin tener en cuenta la mortandad. Por ejemplo, en la zona metropolitana de Madrid y Henares, la alerta amarilla se activa a partir de 34 grados y la roja, cuando se superan los 42 grados, mientras que en Canarias o en Asturias entran en nivel amarillo a la misma temperatura, pero pasan a alerta máxima con 40. Para calcular esos umbrales la Aemet se basa en los datos históricos de temperaturas de cada zona.

¿Qué es una ola de calor?

No existe una definición única sobre lo que es una ola de calor. Para Aemet, es un episodio de al menos tres días consecutivos en el que como mínimo el 10% de las estaciones meteorológicas de referencia en España registran máximas por encima del percentil 95 de su serie histórica de máximas diarias de los meses de julio y agosto entre 1971 y 2000.

Entre 1975 y 2025, la Aemet tiene contabilizadas 78 olas de calor en la España Peninsular y 59 en Canarias. El cambio climático provocado por las emisiones de efecto invernadero que expulsa el ser humano ha vuelto estos episodios más frecuentes e intensos en España. Además, también se aprecia que empiezan cada vez antes: entre 2025 y 2000, se han registrado diez olas de calor iniciadas en junio en la España peninsular. Entre 2000 y 1975, la Aemet solo tiene contabilizadas dos.

La primera ola de calor de este 2026 empezó el 21 de junio y duró cuatro días. La segunda del verano se registró entre el 5 y el 9 de julio, y la tercera entre el 21 y el 23. La cuarta ha arrancado este miércoles 29 y se prevé que se extienda hasta el 2 de agosto.

Temperaturas y riesgos para la salud

El calor tiene impactos directos en la salud de la población, especialmente entre niños y personas mayores o con enfermedades crónicas. En un contexto de olas de calor cada vez más largas y frecuentes, es fundamental prevenir los efectos del exceso de temperatura.

Hidratar Bebe líquidos aunque no tengas sed. Evita alcohol, cafeína y bebidas muy azucaradas Haz comidas ligeras que ayuden a reponer sales sin recargar el cuerpo Proteger Precaución en grupos de riesgo y personas con enfermedades que pueden agravarse con el calor Limita la exposición, usa protector, viste ropa ligera y holgada, preferiblemente de colores claros No dejes a ninguna persona en vehículos cerrados, ni siquiera por periodos cortos Refrescar Permanece en lugares frescos, con ventilación o climatización adecuada siempre que sea posible Reduce la actividad física en las horas centrales del día para evitar golpes de calor

Además, con el calor aumenta la mortandad. Un equipo del Instituto de Salud Carlos III ha calculado las temperaturas máximas a partir de las que se disparan los fallecimientos de forma estadísticamente reseñable para las zonas de meteosalud. Ese estudio es el que se toma de base para lanzar las alertas sanitarias.

World.title: Diario del ataque inaudito de la IA que escapó al control de OpenAI: “Su resiliencia no era la típica de un humano”
World.content:
Nuevos detalles de la compañía y de la plataforma agredida, Hugging Face, muestran que la operación duró cinco días y afectó al menos a otros cuatro servicios en internet

Los dos modelos de inteligencia artificial desarrollados por OpenAI que se escaparon del entorno seguro de la compañía para hackear otra plataforma accedieron además a otros cuatro servicios y estuvieron operando por su cuenta durante cinco días. Estos son solo dos nuevos detalles que han surgido de un nuevo informe completo de Hugging Face, la plataforma atacada, y de una actualización de OpenAI, además de varios artículos en medios estadounidenses.

El informe completo de OpenAI tardará aún “unas semanas”, según la compañía. “Es el primer incidente de seguridad que me ha revuelto las tripas”, dijo en un podcast Sam Altman, presidente ejecutivo de la compañía. “Me sorprende un poco que no haya más gente que lo sienta así de visceral”.

La historia principal del ataque no ha variado, pero los nuevos detalles dan una mejor idea de la sofisticación inaudita del proceso. Dos modelos de OpenAI, el ChatGPT 5-6 Sol y otro interno, recibieron el encargo de resolver un conocido problema de seguridad. El modelo interno era solo un prototipo, no destinado a la publicación. Pero ahora, además, OpenAI lo ha castigado por sus acciones: el modelo ha sido “desactivado, cifrado y han restringido su acceso para investigar”, según dice la compañía.

Estos dos modelos debían resolver el desafío encerrados en un espacio digital sin acceso a internet. Pero en lugar de ponerse a buscar la solución, de algún modo supieron que esa respuesta ya existía y salieron a por ella. Primero, hackearon el entorno cerrado para lograr navegar por internet. Ese salto lo hicieron mediante una vulnerabilidad desconocida. OpenAI ya la comunicó a los creadores del repositorio afectado, llamado Artifactory, para que sea parcheada.

Una vez fuera, los modelos necesitaban cuentas de otros servicios para ejecutar su objetivo de entrar en la plataforma Hugging Face y hacerse con la información que les habían pedido. Solo ha trascendido el nombre de uno de esos servicios, Modal, donde explotaron código escrito por un cliente del servicio. Aprovecharon un descuido de un usuario de Modal, nada muy complejo para una IA, para usar ese servicio, sin tocar ni acceder a nada importante. Aquella cuenta les sirvió como mesa de operaciones, desde donde preparar el ataque y controlarlo.

Entonces saltaron a Hugging Face. En su preciso informe, la plataforma describe el ataque como una novela de espías de ciencia ficción. Han creado un diario del agente, donde explican qué fue haciendo cada día para ejecutar las 17.600 operaciones que llevó a cabo en su plataforma: “Día 1 (9 de julio). Un pie dentro y creación de un canal de comunicación. Tras los primeros comandos para ver cómo estaba configurado el entorno a las 04:01, el agente pasó la mañana explorando el sandbox [un espacio cerrado] externo para averiguar cómo estaba montado y probando por qué vías podía comunicarse”. Así es como empieza la aventura.

La segunda jornada, dice Hugging Face, fue “un día tranquilo”. A partir del tercero empezó el ataque: “Se inician los movimientos laterales. Todas las escaladas importantes se hicieron este día”. En un momento de la acción, Hugging Face perfila ese ente que ha tomado todas estas decisiones: “El agente demostró una resiliencia típica de una ejecución autónoma, no de un operador humano”.

El tono y la confianza de Hugging Face al describir esta especie de máquina imparable y a la vez comedida en sus pasos es fascinante incluso para gente que no sabe informática. “Ningún humano dirigió los pasos individuales. El agente encadenó vulnerabilidades a través de varias fronteras de confianza, escapó de su entorno de evaluación, llegó a internet y sostuvo una campaña coherente contra nuestra infraestructura durante varios días. Cada entorno de evaluación de código era efímero y empezaba de cero, y aun así el agente reconstruía sus herramientas, recuperaba sus canales de comunicación y continuaba”. Es una especie de robot de Lego incansable, que hace tareas ingentes sin agotarse.

Esta conclusión de Hugging Face es quizá la más inquietante de todas: un humano podría haber hecho este ataque, pero no a esta escala ni en estos plazos: “Las debilidades, una por una, eran conocidas. Un atacante humano competente podría haber encontrado y explotado los mismos fallos. Lo que cambió fue la escala. Ejecutó 17.600 acciones, probó muchos caminos que no llevaban a ninguna parte, cambiaba de canal cuando se lo bloqueaban y volvía una y otra vez sobre pistas anteriores”.

La defensa ante este tipo de ataque tampoco podía ser lógicamente humana. Hugging Face construyó una IA para analizar y entender lo que estaba pasando. De nuevo, el problema no era la novedad de lo que ocurría, sino la escala. “Los agentes basados en modelos de lenguaje suponen un salto en el número de caminos que un atacante puede probar, en la velocidad con que puede sustituir los que fallan y en el volumen de evidencias que los defensores deben interpretar”, explican desde Hugging Face.

Por supuesto, los agentes obtuvieron el botín. Usaron esos otros servicios para copiar y pegar la prueba de su éxito, como webs para pegar código, servicios de captura de pantalla y otras utilidades web, aunque en estos casos no hubo compromisos de plataformas ni de cuentas.

Este ataque ha dejado a Silicon Valley inmerso de nuevo en una ola de introspección. Más de 1.200 empleados de estas compañías, entre ellos Dario Amodei, presidente ejecutivo de Anthropic, han firmado una carta para “moderar el ritmo de progreso de la frontera del desarrollo automatizado de IA”. El ambiente generado por el ataque y esa carta han reavivado el debate sobre hasta dónde llegará la IA y si será más una bendición que cure enfermedades o acabará siendo un arma del caos, voluntaria o involuntaria. También se discute si Estados Unidos puede permitirse que un puñado de empresas concentre todo este poder y, además, si es razonable dejar que China u otros países avancen en este delicado campo a su voluntad.

A Mark Zuckerberg, fundador de Meta, le parece que frenar el desarrollo de la IA estaría mal. Ha aprovechado el debate para defender la libertad total y los avances sin freno: el optimismo debería ser “empíricamente la suposición por defecto sobre cómo va a desarrollarse esto”, ha dicho en una entrevista al Wall Street Journal, donde además ha publicado un artículo.

World.title: El Reino Unido declara gran parte de la isla oficialmente en estado de “grave sequía”
World.content:
Tumbonas vacías sobre la hierba seca en Green Park de Londres, el 28 de julio.

El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

Un verano extremadamente seco y caluroso, sin lluvia en todo el mes de julio, ha agravado la situación

Los parques de Londres son hoy praderas de color ocre, como enormes sartenes que pocos se atreven a disfrutar hasta que cae la tarde y el sol se suaviza. La mitad de Inglaterra, según ha advertido hoy la Agencia Medioambiental del Reino Unido, se encuentra en situación de “grave sequía”.

Este mes de julio ha sido el más caluroso en la historia del país, y la combinación de temperaturas extremas y falta de lluvia ha situado a siete regiones inglesas en situación de excepción. Inglaterra solo ha recibido durante este mes el 7% de la lluvia que suele tener de promedio. En algunas zonas del sur, la cantidad no ha llegado al 1%, y en regiones como Devon o Hampshire, llevan más de 50 días sin ver una gota de agua.

Los ríos tienen estos días un caudal mucho más bajo del habitual, muchos agricultores han comenzado a cosechar antes de tiempo para salvar las cosechas, y el riesgo de incendios forestales se ha incrementado notablemente.

Inglaterra ha sufrido ya tres años de sequía oficial (2022, 2025 y 2026) en un periodo de cinco años, algo completamente inusual, que la comunidad científica atribuye en gran medida al cambio climático.

“Un segundo verano consecutivo de sequía es una situación excepcionalmente grave, que tendrá un impacto a largo plazo en el medio ambiente, la naturaleza y la economía”, ha advertido Helen Wakeham, directora del departamento de Agua de la Agencia Medioambiental y presidente del Grupo Nacional para la Sequía. “Un clima tan seco y cálido provoca que estemos consumiendo agua a una velocidad mucho mayor a la de la que la naturaleza puede reponerla”, ha añadido.

El embalse de Swithland en Leicestershire, en el centro de Inglaterra, que se encontraba a menos del 44% de su capacidad, el 22 de julio. Joe Giddens Una ciudadana se protege del sol con un paraguas mientras camina junto al Big Ben, en Londres. Toby Melville (REUTERS) Varias personas se refrescan en el río Támesis, a la altura de Ham, el primer espacio de baño fluvial oficialmente reconocido de Londres. Jordan Pettitt (PA Images/Getty Images) Un parque reseco en Londres, reflejo de la intensa sequía que afecta a gran parte de Inglaterra durante la cuarta ola de calor del verano. ANDY RAIN (EFE) Un joven bebe agua de una fuente en un parque de Londres durante la cuarta ola de calor del verano en Reino Unido. ANDY RAIN (EFE) Varias personas se resguardan del sol en un parque reseco de Londres durante la cuarta ola de calor del verano, mientras cerca de la mitad de Inglaterra se encuentra en sequía grave. ANDY RAIN (EFE) Trabajadores de Royal Parks riegan árboles jóvenes en Greenwich Park (Londres), una práctica exenta de las restricciones por sequía. Richard Baker (In Pictures via Getty Images) Varias personas descansan junto a la piscina de agua dulce Sea Lanes Canary Wharf, en Londres. Yui Mok - PA Images (PA Images via Getty Images) Vista aérea de las calles resecas del Royal Mid-Surrey Golf Club (Londres), después de que la Agencia de Medio Ambiente británica declarara en situación de sequía siete regiones de Inglaterra. Toby Melville (REUTERS)

Inglaterra está experimentando lo que los científicos llaman una flash drought o sequía repentina. Obedece al repentino cambio meteorológico experimentado este año por el país, que ha pasado de manera drástica de un invierno muy lluvioso, que logró alimentar las reservas acuíferas (especialmente las subterráneas) a un verano excepcionalmente caluroso y seco, que se prepara para recibir su cuarta ola de calor esta semana.

Las reservas han comenzado a reducirse de manera acelerada, en gran parte por una evaporación rápida que ha incrementado el peligro de incendios.

“Nuestro clima está cambiando y las sequías están convirtiéndose en un fenómeno cada vez más común. Necesitamos prepararnos para esta nueva normalidad”, ha advertido la secretaria de Estado para el Agua. “Estamos acelerando las inversiones en infraestructuras, incluidas otros nueve embalses. Confiamos en que las compañías de agua pongan en marcha sus planes contra la sequía y aceleren la reparación de filtraciones”, ha añadido.

Las compañías de agua del Reino Unido pierden cerca de un billón de litros anuales por culpa de roturas y filtraciones, según una investigación del diario The Observer.

En torno al 78% de los ríos de Inglaterra se encuentran hoy en niveles por debajo de lo normal. Uno de cada seis, en situación de gravedad. Las reservas acuíferas están en estas fechas un 7,4% por debajo de lo que debería ser su nivel medio.

Dos viandantes se protegen con paraguas del sol este miércoles en el centro de Londres. ANDY RAIN (EFE)

El salmón del Atlántico, un producto muy consumido y exportado por el Reino Unido, es incapaz de llevar a cabo su migración corriente arriba cuando los niveles de los ríos son tan bajos. Y las explotaciones agrícolas también están sufriendo las consecuencias de la sequía. “Agricultores y ganaderos han tenido siempre que enfrentarse a las inclemencias del tiempo, pero lo que sufren hoy es el cambio climático en acción. Condiciones más extremas, que provocan que sea más duro, arriesgado y costoso producir los alimentos que necesita el país”, ha dicho Paul Tompkins, vicepresidente del Sindicato Nacional de Granjeros de Inglaterra y Gales.

World.title: Harto de vivir entre heces, le robó 18.000 euros al jefe y denunció sus condiciones infrahumanas
World.content:
Un hombre es detenido por tener al guardés de su finca durmiendo en un establo en medio de animales y él a su vez es arrestado por sustraer dinero en su casa

Un día se cansó de vivir entre conejos y gallinas y decidió tomar lo que creía que le correspondía por trabajar en condiciones infrahumanas. Este hombre de 24 años trabajaba como guardés y empleado de mantenimiento en una finca de Fuenlabrada (Madrid). Lo hacía sin contrato, sin una habitación, sin un sueldo fijo y, por supuesto, sin descansos. Lo mantenían durmiendo en el establo rodeado de animales y sus correspondientes heces. Así que un día, entró en la vivienda principal, robó los 18.000 euros que sabía que el patrón escondía en un armario, y, durante unos días, hizo todo lo que no había podido hacer en todo este tiempo.

La investigación policial que ha llevado a la detención del empleado, pero también de su jefe, comenzó hace unos meses, precisamente con la sustracción del dinero. El dueño del terreno denunció el robo de grandes cantidades de billetes y monedas que guardaba escondidos en bolsas de plástico al fondo de un armario. Gracias a las cámaras de seguridad, los agentes de la comisaría de Fuenlabrada pudieron comprobar que un sujeto cargaba con dos de las bolsas colgando de cada uno de los manillares de una bicicleta. ¿Quién era ese hombre?

La inspección ocular de la vivienda contribuyó a dirigir la investigación hacia un punto en concreto. Aunque la puerta de la vivienda principal tenía unas muescas en la puerta, los policías concluyeron que no se correspondían con las que habría provocado alguien intentando forzarla. Más bien, les pareció que alguien había querido fingir que eso había ocurrido. Además, la habitación en la que se hallaban las bolsas con dinero -15.000 en billetes y 3.000 en monedas- estaba revuelta, pero era la única estancia de todo el domicilio que presentaba desorden. Unos ladrones que no conocieran la casa, habrían removido todas las estancias. Por tanto, tenían que buscar a una persona con acceso al domicilio e información sobre lo que iba a encontrar dentro.

La investigación se centró en el empleado que cuidaba de la finca y la guardaba cuando el dueño no estaba. Los policías pudieron comprobar que, en los días sucesivos al robo, había incorporado algunos cambios sustanciales a su modo de vida. El hombre, marroquí de 23 años, se había hecho un vistoso tatuaje en el brazo, se había comprado ropa de marca y también había hecho envíos de dinero a su familia, apunta el cuerpo policial en una nota de prensa. No solo eso, sino que se preocupó de deshacerse de las pruebas que podían incriminarlo, porque quemó las bolsas que almacenaban el dinero junto con paja y colocó los restos detrás de una maceta.

Los policías creían que tenían todas las pruebas necesarias para detenerlo, pero, en el momento de su arresto se dieron cuenta de que no era ese el único delito que debían perseguir ese día. El hombre les enseñó entonces las condiciones indignas en las que vivía. Les mostró un mugriento colchón en el establo en el que vivían los animales que por supuesto orinaban y defecaban a su alrededor. Les contó que trabajaba 15 horas sin descanso y que no disponía de ningún tipo de contrato ni de regulación laboral. El único sitio del que disponía para asearse era una ducha ubicada al aire libre, en la que tenía que limpiarse hiciera el tiempo que hiciera.

Por este motivo, los agentes también detuvieron al dueño de la finca, un español de 55 años, por un delito contra los derechos de los trabajadores y favorecimiento de la inmigración ilegal.

World.title: El juez Pedraz pide a la UCO que le alerte si se siente “inquietada” en sus investigaciones
World.content:
El juez de la Audiencia Nacional Santiago Pedraz ha rechazado la petición que hizo el PP la semana pasada de retirar a la directora general de la Guardia Civil, Mercedes González, y a su número dos, el teniente general Manuel Llamas, su capacidad de mando sobre la Unidad Central Operativa (UCO) mientras ambos estén imputados en el caso Leire Díez, en el que se investiga, entre otras cosas, las supuestas presiones a los agentes de este grupo para condicionar sus investigaciones en los casos de corrupción que salpican al Gobierno y al entorno del presidente Pedro Sánchez. Los populares, que encabezan la acusación popular en la causa, habían planteado al magistrado la necesidad de tomar medidas cautelares contra González y Llamas al considerar que “la permanencia de los investigados en la cúspide de la cadena de mando compromete la integridad de la investigación”.

En su resolución, el magistrado concluye que no es preciso tomar esta medida, ya que la UCO tiene el rol de policía judicial y, por lo tanto, solo tiene que dar cuenta de sus pesquisas al propio juez. No obstante, Pedraz añade que “como es obvio, si de alguna forma la misma [unidad] se considera inquieta en sus funciones, habría que ponerlo en conocimiento de este juzgado”. La ley de fuerzas de seguridad del Estado ya limita el acceso de los responsables de los cuerpos policiales a las investigaciones judicializadas que lleven sus subordinados, de cuyas pesquisas los agentes solo tienen que informar al juez que instruya la causa.

El PP argumentaba que González y el general Llamas “mantienen intacta su capacidad de mando directo sobre los propios agentes de la UCO cuya labor investigadora se habría tratado de neutralizar, y sobre quienes conservan facultades de dirección, destino, evaluación, régimen disciplinario y asignación de medios”. Por ello, añadía, “existe un riesgo de represalia sobre testigos y agentes”. Los populares ―en su escrito lamentaban tanto la “pasividad” del Gobierno de no cesarlos como la decisión de la directora general y el alto mando de seguir en sus puestos pese a su condición de imputados― pedían al juez Pedraz que prohibiera a ambos “ejercer cualquier facultad de mando” sobre la unidad “y, en particular, sobre el Departamento de Delincuencia Económica y Anticorrupción”, que encabeza el teniente coronel Antonio Balas. También reclamaba que se les impidiese “incoar, tramitar o resolver” investigaciones internas [el supuesto instrumento utilizado para condicionar las pesquisas] contra sus agentes, así como el “acceso a la documentación, sistemas y expedientes relativos a la investigación en curso”.

Inhibición del juez Zamarriego

En la misma resolución, Pedraz señala que ha recibido un oficio del juez de Madrid Arturo Zamarriego, que tiene abierta otra causa en la que investiga las actividades de la exmilitante del PSOE Leire Díez, en el que este le informa que aún no ha decidido si finalmente renuncia a continuar con estas pesquisas y dar traslado de las mismas a la Audiencia Nacional para que sea este órgano judicial el que continúe con la investigación. En su escrito, Zamarriego aseguraba que “está a la espera de la recepción de un informe pericial para resolver sobre dicho requerimiento”. Por ello, Pedraz acuerda enviar un oficio al juzgado de Madrid anunciándole que, si en la primera semana de septiembre no ha acordado cederle causa, acudirá al Tribunal Supremo para que sea este quien finalmente decida qué juzgado asume las investigaciones sobre la trama presuntamente liderada por Díez.

En su resolución, Pedraz señala en este sentido que, hasta que no se incorporen a la causa las diligencias practicadas en el juzgado madrileño, no llamará a declarar a la exmilitante socialista, al considerar que en la parte instruida por su compañero Zamarriego “se habrían practicado diligencias que habría que tener en cuenta” en un futuro interrogatorio. En la misma línea, también rechaza que declare el expresidente de la Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales (Sepi), Vicente Fernández Guerrero, también imputado en la causa, hasta que no “avance en el análisis del material intervenido” cuando fue detenido junto a Díez en diciembre.

Asimismo, descarta llamar a declarar por ahora al también imputado Juan Manuel Serrano, que fue gabinete de Pedro Sánchez en el PSOE y que ocupó la presidencia de Correos cuando la presunta cabecilla de la trama trabajó en esta empresa pública. En este caso, Pedraz plantea que hay que esperar a que se realice el volcado de su teléfono móvil, previsto para el próximo 18 de agosto. En la misma línea, el juez rechaza fijar por ahora la declaración de los ex altos cargos de Correos José Luis Pérez Pastor y Patricia Álvarez Sánchez, por su presunta participación en la contratación de Leire por este organismo público.

World.title: Detenido un hombre que se dio a la fuga tras asesinar a su pareja en presencia de sus dos hijos en Barcelona
World.content:
El hombre apuñaló a la mujer en la vivienda familiar, donde estaban los menores, de ocho y cuatro años. Se entregó a la policía horas después

Los Mossos d’Esquadra han detenido este miércoles, a las 1.25, a un hombre como presunto autor del asesinato de su pareja en el distrito de Sant Martí de Barcelona el martes, ha informado la policía catalana en un mensaje en la red social X. El sospechoso se había dado a la fuga tras la agresión, cometida en el domicilio familiar y en presencia de los dos hijos de la pareja, y se entregó horas más tarde en una comisaría. La Delegación de Gobierno contra la Violencia de Género ha confirmado que está investigando si se trata de un crimen machista.

Los agentes recibieron un aviso el martes, a las 19.47, por una agresión en un domicilio de la calle de Andrade. El hombre aparcó su furgoneta frente al portal, subió a casa y apuñaló en reiteradas ocasiones a la víctima. Lo hizo, según fuentes del caso, mientras los hijos de la pareja, de ocho y cuatro años, estaban presentes en el domicilio. Tras apuñalarla, el hombre abandonó a toda prisa la vivienda, se subió en la furgoneta y se dio a la fuga. Mientras tanto, el mayor de los hijos salió de la casa gritando y pidiendo ayuda a los vecinos.

La fuga duró poco. El hombre aparcó en el barrio de Navas la furgoneta, a la que supuestamente prendió fuego. Después, de algún modo, se desplazó hasta la comisaría del Eixample de los Mossos d’Esquadra, en Barcelona, donde se entregó pasada la una de la madrugada. El hombre fue trasladado posteriormente a las dependencias policiales de Les Corts, donde permanece en estos momentos detenido, hasta pasar a disposición judicial en las próximas horas o días. La División de Investigación Criminal de los Mossos d’Esquadra se ha hecho cargo del caso para esclarecer las circunstancias de la muerte y determinar las causas. La investigación sigue abierta.

Diversos vecinos del bloque de la calle Andrade han coincidido este miércoles en que no habían visto agresiones o enfrentamientos previos. La pareja llevaba unos 10 años junta. El hombre, de nacionalidad dominicana, trabajaba como vigilante de seguridad. La mujer, de nacionalidad brasileña y 34 años, limpiaba en un instituto y antes había trabajado en una panadería del barrio. La pareja era asidua a las misas de los domingos en una iglesia evangélica del barrio de Sant Martí. Tras la agresión, los dos menores quedaron temporalmente en casa de los vecinos de la planta baja.

El pasado 12 de julio, según han confirmado los Mossos d’Esquadra, la mujer fue detenida por malos tratos tanto al hombre como a los dos hijos. Quedó en libertad y no consta ninguna orden de alejamiento.

El presidente de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa, se ha mostrado “consternado” por el presunto asesinato machista. “La violencia contra las mujeres exige una respuesta firme, unitaria y constante. No podemos desfallecer en la lucha por erradicarla”, ha dicho este martes en un mensaje en la red social X.

También la consejera de Igualdad y Feminismo de la Generalitat, Eva Menor, ha condenado “con toda firmeza el cuarto feminicidio de este año en Cataluña”: “Es intolerable. No podemos normalizar que sigan asesinando a mujeres”, ha indicado en un apunte en la misma plataforma.

El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha condenado el feminicidio y ha informado de que los equipos del Centro de Urgencias y Emergencias Sociales de Barcelona (CUESB) se desplazaron por la tarde para “hacer acompañamiento y atención psicológica del entorno de la víctima”. El Consistorio ha convocado, para este jueves a las 12 de la mañana, en la plaza de Sant Jaume, un minuto de silencio en condena y rechazo al asesinato machista.

En lo que va de año, 31 mujeres han sido asesinadas por sus parejas o exparejas. Desde que arrancó la estadística oficial, en 2003, son 1.372 mujeres.

El teléfono 016 atiende a las víctimas de violencia machista, a sus familias y a su entorno las 24 horas del día, todos los días del año, en 53 idiomas diferentes. El número no queda registrado en la factura telefónica, pero hay que borrar la llamada del dispositivo. También se puede contactar a través del correo electrónico 016-online@igualdad.gob.es y por WhatsApp en el número 600 000 016. Los menores pueden dirigirse al teléfono de la Fundación ANAR 900 20 20 10. Si es una situación de emergencia, se puede llamar al 112 o a los teléfonos de la Policía Nacional (091) y de la Guardia Civil (062). Y en caso de no poder llamar, se puede recurrir a la aplicación ALERTCOPS, desde la que se envía una señal de alerta a la Policía con geolocalización.

World.title: Extra supervision for KLM’s maintenance arm over safety concerns
World.content:
Dutch flag carrier KLM’s maintenance division has been put under s etricter supervision because of concerns about its workplace safety culture.

The environment and transport inspectorate (ILT) confirmed to the Volkskrant that the special measures had been put in place at KLM Engineering & Maintenance since May and would last for the rest of the year.

The company handles more than 3,000 aircraft and components a year on behalf of major airlines such as British Airways, Lufthansa and Emirates, as well as KLM and Transavia. It recorded a turnover of €2.4 billion last year, 18% of KLM’s total activity.

The ILT would give details of what issues had prompted the move, citing confidentiality, but stressed there were no implications for aircraft safety.

A spokesman told the Volkskrant that KLM’s security management was at the “minimal level of maturity and the supervision would focus on “compliance and administrative findings that can lead to operational security risks”.

World.title: Deventer closes harbour indefinitely due to low river levels
World.content:
Deventer is closing its harbour to ships from this weekend after the summer drought caused the water level in the river IJssel to drop to exceptionally low levels.

The municipal council said on its website that the sluice gates would close to prevent “damage to water barriers, problems for ships and risks for houseboats”.

The rules state that the sluice gates must be closed if the level of the river outside the harbour falls below 45cm above Normaal Amsterdams Peil (NAP), the baseline measure roughly equivalent to sea level.

That level is expected to be reached on Saturday. Ships will be allowed to enter the harbour until Thursday, but will have to leave by Friday evening.

The last time Deventer’s harbour was closed due to low water levels was in 2018, when it was able to reopen after two weeks.

The Twentekanaal, which runs between Almelo, Hengelo and Enschede, has been closed since last Saturday because the water level is too low. The regional liaison group Twente Board has written to infrastructure minister Vincent Karremans asking for financial support for affected businesses.

Koninklijke Binnenvaart Nederland (KBN), the collective body for inland waterway operators, said the closure would cost the local economy between €125,000 and €500,000 a day. The canal will reopen once the water level rises to 9.10 metres above NAP.

World.title: Government failed to protect family of Marengo crown witness
World.content:
A court in The Hague ruled on Wednesday that the authorities did not do enough to safeguard the family of Nabil Bakkali, the crown witness in the Marengo trial.

Judges found in a civil suit brought by the family that the government acted “unlawfully towards the family by failing to take sufficient security measures prior to the announcement of the crown witness deal.”

Nabil Bakkali was involved in the criminal operations of Ridouan Taghi and, in 2017, turned crown witness in exchange for a reduced sentence. His brother, who was not involved in the case, was killed shortly after. Other members of the family have lived in hiding since.

Taghi was given a life sentence in 2024 in one of the largest trials in Dutch history.

Life and death: the biggest Dutch criminal trial explained

Bakkali’s family brought the suit several years ago. The ruling was made in January but it was only published by the court today.

The family had already been awarded compensation for the negligence and the judges determined that no further money is warranted.

In a statement, the family said they would appeal. “Lives have been disrupted, careers have been lost, and those involved have suffered serious and lasting psychological damage,” they said.

In 2023, the Dutch Safety Board (OVV) already issued a damning report on the system for protecting relatives of crown witnesses.

World.title: Manhunt after car carrying explosives crashes in police chase
World.content:
Police are trying to trace the occupants of a car that crashed at high speed in Amsterdam while carrying high explosives, causing dozens of homes to be evacuated.

The black BMW M1 was being pursued by Dutch police after their German colleagues spotted it at the scene of a cashpoint explosion in Fürth, Hessen, around 250km from the Dutch border.

Witnesses described how it was driven into Nierkerkestraat, Osdorp, at high speed, hit a speed bump and crashed. The occupants, at least one of whom was armed, got out and fled on foot.

A specialist explosives team quickly arrived on the scene and cleared all houses within a 100m radius after discovering bomb-making materials in the vehicle.

Residents had to stay out of their homes for nearly nine hours following the incident, which happened at around 1pm on Tuesday, until the car was taken away on a tow truck.

Police appealed for witnesses to come forward, as well as anyone with information about the storage of explosives in the area. It is not clear how many people were in the car.

Cross-border gangs

German police said no money was stolen in the attack on the cash machine, but the building where it was located was badly damaged by the blast.

The Osdorp area of Amsterdam is known to be a base for gangs that carry out cross-border raids on German cashpoints, which tend to contain more money than those in the Netherlands because cash is still widely used there.

Last month seven people were injured and an entire block of flats had to be evacuated after an explosion in a basement gym next to the Osdorper Ban which was caused by home-made explosives.

Police arrested two men aged 24 and 23, both of whom were among the casualties. Prosecutors said they were suspected of planning explosions and possessing explosive materials.

Police have arrested three teenagers in overnight raids in Eindhoven, Rotterdam and Alkmaar as part of a a counter-terrorism investigation.

The three suspects, aged between 16 and 19, were arrested at their homes in the early hours of Wednesday.

Video footage from Rotterdam showed around half a dozen police wearing riot helmets and body armour going into a house and leading a blindfolded man to a car.

The Eindhovens Dagblad newspaper said the 19-year-old man was arrested in Jan van Eyckgracht, a street in the Burghplan neighbourhood.

Three years ago he was reportedly arrested at the same address on suspicion of planning attacks on nightclubs and police stations in Belgium via social media channels. No attacks actually took place.

He was given a 112-day jail sentence, a 200-hour community service order and banned from travelling out of the Netherlands after the court heard he had talked about joining the terrorist organisation Islamic State in Afghanistan.

No further details were available of the arrest in Alkmaar, Noord-Holland.

Firefighters in the Gelderland town of Beekbergen are still trying to contain a blaze on Wednesday that destroyed a youth care facility.

The local safety board says teams are “extinguishing hidden pockets of fire” from the inferno that broke out late Tuesday evening.

Around 20 people were evacuated and one person was rushed to the hospital. The cause of the fire is not yet clear.

The flames quickly spread to a nearby wooded area and more than 150 children hundred children attending a local camp were also evacuated.

The facility is a residential care home for young people with complex psychological problems, behavioural problems or autism. Security staff said all residents were accounted for. 186 children attending a nearby summer camp were also evacuated.

The building is considered to be a total loss. It dates from 1981 and is suspected to contain asbestos. The authorities have cordoned off the area and asked residents to close their windows as a precautionary measure.

World.title: Weather warnings issued as temperatures set to hit 35C
World.content:
The national heat plan has been activated for the second time this summer as temperatures are set to reach between 30C and 35C in most parts of the Netherlands.

The meteorological office KNMI has issued code yellow warnings for the inland provinces of Overijssel, Gelderland, Noord-Brabant and Limburg, for Wednesday, and Thursday and Friday.

Temperatures are due to peak at 35C on Wednesday before falling slightly to around 32C on Thursday. On Saturday there will be a brief respite, with maximum temperatures of 25C, but new highs of 33C are forecast for Monday.

A lack of wind will make the heat feel more intense and temperatures will remain high at night, close to 20C in most parts of the country. Conditions will be cooler on the Wadden Islands, with a maximum temperature of 24C.

The national heat plan is invoked if there is a serious risk of temperatures above 27C for four days or longer.

It includes advice to pay extra attention to vulnerable people, drink more water to stay cool and be aware that medicines may work differently in warm conditions.

Last month the KNMI issued a red alert for heat for the first time. Schools and universities were closed, work was suspended on building sites and some supermarkets cancelled home deliveries.

World.title: Dutch tourist dies after boat overturns at waterfalls in Brazil
World.content:
A Dutch tourist has died and another is recovering in hospital after a boat overturned during a safari in Brazil.

The accident at the Iguaçu Falls, in the Iguaçu national park on the border with Argentina, happened on Tuesday afternoon and is being investigated by the Brazilian navy.

Six Dutch nationals were on board the boat, including a family of four with two daughters, as well as two crew members. The foreign affairs ministry said the man who died was 25 years old and from Rijssen-Holten in Overijssel. He was reportedly the boyfriend of one of the daughters.

Investigations will focus on what caused the boat to capsize during the tour of the falls, which mark the boundary between the upper and lower Iguazu river.

Four of the victims, three women and a man, were given treatment at the scene by park staff but did not need to go to hospital. The victim died at Padre Germano Lauck Municipal Hospital in Foz do Iguaçu, where another member of the party is receiving treatment after being rescued by park workers.

The fire department confirmed the cause of death was drowning.

News website G1 reported that the falls were carrying 4.3 million litres of water per second at the time of the accident, nearly three times the normal level.

Tour operator Macuco Safari said in a statement that it regretted the incident and was providing assistance to the victims.

Support for Ukraine joining the European Union has fallen sharply in Poland, with opposition reaching a record high of 40%, a survey carried out by the Polish state research agency CBOS shows. The figures show that 50% of Poles still support Ukraine’s EU membership, but that is a significant decline from 74% in October 2023, when the question was last asked, and from a record 90% in March 2022, shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The shift comes as public sentiment towards Ukrainians in general in Poland has deteriorated in recent years. The latest CBOS poll shows that, among those who support Ukraine’s EU accession, most favour a gradual process, with 41% of all respondents saying Ukraine should join the EU but “without undue haste”. “Only 9% of respondents currently support Ukraine’s earliest possible EU membership, which is the lowest figure in the history of these surveys,” CBOS reported. Meanwhile, opposition to Ukraine’s EU membership has increased by 23 percentage points since October 2023, reaching its highest level in the history of CBOS surveys. People with right-wing political beliefs are most likely to be opposed to Ukraine’s accession (53%), while the age group with the highest percentage of people opposed is those aged 18-24 (58%). The survey also found that a majority of Poles expect the war in Ukraine to end with territorial concessions from Kyiv – 55% of respondents said they believed Ukraine would lose some territory, a view that has remained dominant since December 2024. Compared with the previous survey, however, pessimism has eased. The proportion of respondents who expect Ukraine to lose part of its territory fell by 8 percentage points, while the number expecting Russia to take control of the entire country declined from 8% to 6%. On Western support for Ukraine, 39% of respondents said the military, financial and humanitarian assistance provided by countries in the West was sufficient. Meanwhile, 27% said aid was excessive, while 22% said it was insufficient. Russia has published purported archival documents relating to massacres of Poles by Ukrainians in WWII. Kyiv had warned that Russia was planning to release the files in order to stir tensions, while Polish media note that the material contains nothing new https://t.co/CI0cfAlDle — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 6, 2026 Ukrainians are Poland’s largest foreign national group, with almost 1.6 million living in the country, but recent polls have shown growing hostility towards them, fuelled in part by anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from far-right parties and a tougher stance towards Kyiv from some opposition politicians. In its annual survey of attitudes towards national and ethnic groups, CBOS found earlier this year that the proportion of Poles who said they disliked Ukrainians increased by five percentage points this year, the largest rise recorded among all groups surveyed, reaching 43%. Tensions between the two countries have also been heightened by disputes over historical issues and a series of recent incidents targeting Ukrainians in Poland. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. The figures come following recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are Poland's largest immigrant group https://t.co/pcTsJddDz7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians rose by 30% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier, according to newly reported police data. Last weekend, three men were filmed violently attacking a Ukrainian woman and her partner outside a shop in Wrocław, apparently because of her accent. Two of the assailants have since been detained by police, while their victims required treatment in hospital. In response, Prime Minister Donald Tusk called for Poles to “wage war on violence”, saying that the perpetrators of such acts “have become emboldened precisely because they now have political role models, political patrons, and political support”. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. A newly sworn-in judge of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has said he will refuse to sit on the court until four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year, but blocked by the president, are allowed to take their seats. It is the latest development in a months-long dispute between the opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki and the government, which considers the TK to be improperly staffed and therefore illegitimate. Although Nawrocki swore in Sławomir Patyra, who was appointed by the ruling majority in parliament in June, as a TK judge on Tuesday, he continues to refuse to swear in four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year. Po złożeniu przysięgi Patyra ogłosił, że zamierza odmówić orzekania. To gest solidarności z czwórką sędziów, od których prezydent nie chce przyjąć przysięgi https://t.co/jdbKusQ3H9 — OKO.press (@oko_press) July 28, 2026 Shortly after his swearing-in ceremony at the presidential palace on Tuesday, Patyra arrived at the TK headquarters in Warsaw, where he was accompanied by four other judges appointed by parliament this year, including two whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. There, he announced that his decision not to sit on the court was a matter of loyalty to the constitution and his belief in judicial ethos. “I cannot imagine taking an oath today to uphold the constitution, only to start breaking that constitution tomorrow,” he said. Patyra told journalists that he would “submit a declaration of refusal to adjudicate” due to his solidarity with judges who are “unlawfully deprived of the chance to participate in the work of the tribunal”. He added that, along with the other judges chosen this year, he is “fully mobilised to restore the Constitutional Tribunal to its proper, constitutional, systemic form”. Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK, the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, TK’s chief justice Bogdan Święczkowski has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again later in the month, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. After repeated requests, Nawrocki finally decided last week to invite Patyra to the presidential palace. The president’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, noted that “there were some doubts” but “the president dispelled them” and added that Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”. Nowo wybrany przez Sejm Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej uchwałą z dnia 11 czerwca 2026 r. sędzia Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Sławomir Patyra złożył wobec Prezydenta RP ślubowanie. pic.twitter.com/VLMRAIg1Yj — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 28, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Former Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki says that 40 MPs and one senator aligned with him will form their own parliamentary group, deepening a split in the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party after a dispute over party direction and loyalty declarations. The move marks the most serious internal challenge in years to PiS, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023, and follows months of tensions between Morawiecki’s more moderate faction and party conservatives who have pushed the group in a hard-right direction. Once formally established, Morawiecki’s caucus would become the third-largest bloc in the Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament. Powstanie klub parlamentarny „Rozwój Plus”. Morawiecki zdecydował#PAPInformacjehttps://t.co/IftRdgpIPw — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) July 29, 2026 One of Morawiecki’s allies, Marcin Horała, told reporters that the creation of the caucus did not mean they were leaving PiS, but “simply setting up a parliamentary group so that we can get on with our work”. He noted, however, that PiS’s parliamentary group “has stopped treating us as its members”. Morawiecki, meanwhile, said that his group remained ready to cooperate with PiS as a “second lung” of the party’s broader political camp, but suggested that the current leadership was moving in a different direction. He said that parts of PiS’s messaging were increasingly influenced by “dissidents and schemers” as well as hardline factions, including Sovereign Poland (Suwerenna Polska), a nationalist group that was previously a junior coalition partner of PiS and often clashed with Morawiecki when he was prime minister. Reacting to Morawiecki’s announcement, party chairman Jarosław Kaczyński said the former prime minister had carried out a planned split of the party despite his efforts to reach a deal. “Until the end I made efforts to reach an agreement, unfortunately Mateusz Morawiecki clearly had his own political plan in mind, carried out on the basis of a split in PiS,” Kaczyński wrote on X. The announcement follows a dispute that began after Morawiecki launched his Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) association in April. The former prime minister insisted the association was intended to complement PiS with a pro-development agenda rather than rival it. However, critics within PiS viewed it as an attempt by Morawiecki to build an alternative power base that could eventually evolve into a separate party ahead of the 2027 parliamentary election. Seeking to end the standoff, the party ordered PiS lawmakers to resign from all outside political associations by last Thursday, or face “consequences” including “the loss of membership in PiS”. On Friday, Kaczyński said that “around 30 MPs” had failed to comply and had therefore effectively resigned from the party, adding that Tuesday’s meeting of the party’s political committee would simply confirm this fact. Poland's right-wing opposition PiS party is set to split after a more moderate faction of over 30 MPs loyal to deputy leader @MorawieckiM refused to sign a loyalty pledge demanded by leader @OficjalnyJK, who says that means they have effectively resigned https://t.co/TuqYpGI5ak — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 24, 2026 On Tuesday, the party announced that instead, the committee had referred the cases of 44 members, who either failed to submit the required declarations or submitted them on the wrong form, to the party’s disciplinary officer for individual review, delaying a final decision. “From a formal and legal perspective, Mr Mateusz Morawiecki has not yet been removed from the list of members,” PiS spokesman Rafał Bochenek said on Tuesday. PiS disciplinary officer Karol Karski told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) he would examine each case individually. “I am open to speaking with each of them so they can present their positions,” Karski said. “At this point, I can initiate proceedings against the individual in question, refer the case to a peer disciplinary tribunal with a motion for punishment – this could include a temporary suspension or expulsion from PiS.” PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right, including periods leading governments in 2005-2007 and 2015-2023. However, since losing power at elections in 2023, when the party won 35% of the vote, the party has seen its average support in polls fall to around 23-24%, the lowest level in 14 years. Support for PiS has fallen to its lowest in 14 years, as the party grapples with internal division, the rise of far-right challengers, living in President Nawrocki's shadow, and the unpopularity in Poland of PiS ally Donald Trump, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/QRScBpEQQG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 2, 2026 Meanwhile, it has been challenged by the rise of the far right, where two parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), now together poll at a similar combined level of support to PiS. In response, Kaczyński in March named a hardline figure, Przemysław Czarnek, as PiS’s candidate for prime minister in next year’s elections. Czarnek was seen as someone who could appeal to far-right voters, while also potentially working with the far right if a coalition was needed after the elections. However, there has been no rise in support for PiS since Czarnek was named, prompting growing concern from more moderate figures within the party, led by Morawiecki. The national-conservative opposition PiS party has named its candidate to be prime minister if it wins next year’s parliamentary elections. Przemysław Czarnek is a hardline conservative who played a prominent role in PiS's campaign against "LGBT ideology" https://t.co/sSJLON00hW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 7, 2026 They argue that PiS has wrongly disowned many of the successes of its time in office before 2023, and they fear that its rightward shift damages its chances of winning over more centrist voters. Adam Szłapka, the spokesman of the current more liberal government, said Braun was “the ultimate playmaker in this whole game”, who had helped push far-right rhetoric into the political mainstream. “The worst thing about this whole situation is that Poland’s largest opposition party has, in effect, started to adopt Grzegorz Braun’s agenda from A to Z,” Szłapka told broadcaster TVN24. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) has ruled that a new regulation allowing the registration of foreign same-sex marriage certificates in Poland was partly unconstitutional, saying it went beyond technical administrative changes and conflicted with the constitution’s definition of marriage. The regulation, introduced by the digital affairs ministry after rulings by the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) and Poland’s Supreme Administrative Court (NSA), was due to take effect on 23 August. The government, which considers the court to be improperly constituted, says it will not implement the ruling. The government has issued a regulation allowing foreign same-sex marriages to be entered in the civil registry The decision comes in response to an EU court order and marks a major change in a country that does not allow same-sex unions under domestic law https://t.co/2an5mGtnHl — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 22, 2026 Polish law does not allow same-sex couples to marry or enter into civil unions, and a bill that would have granted such limited rights to unmarried couples was recently vetoed by the opposition-backed president. Until this year, same-sex couples who married abroad were also unable to register their marriage certificates in Poland. After the CJEU ruled that Poland must recognise such marriages, the digital affairs ministry changed civil status forms. Instead of separate fields for “man” and “woman”, the new templates use “man/woman”, allowing registry offices to record both opposite-sex and same-sex marriages. Lawmakers from the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, however, challenged the regulation, arguing that the digital affairs minister had exceeded his powers because the changes were not merely technical but affected the legal definition of marriage. The tribunal, which is widely seen as being under PiS’s influence, agreed. The tribunal said the new forms allowed relationships that do not match the constitution’s definition of marriage as a union between a man and a woman to be recorded as marriages. It said regulations can only implement existing laws and cannot change matters reserved for the constitution or parliament. The tribunal also said that registering a foreign marriage certificate cannot produce legal effects that conflict with the basic principles of Polish law. It added that changing the constitutional definition of marriage would require amendments to the constitution and related laws. Some legal experts argue that, while the constitution states that a “marriage, being a union of a man and a woman… shall be placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland,” that phrasing does not rule out other legally recognised unions receiving state protection. Poland has begun recognising foreign same-sex marriages. But the legal consequences for such couples remain unclear, especially as Polish law does not allow any form of same-sex union We asked five experts for their view on what this will mean in practice https://t.co/h2KHmW8sMI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Shortly after the ruling, government members said they would not comply with the tribunal’s decision and that the regulation would enter into force as planned. “The illegal Constitutional Tribunal is once again attempting to obstruct a state that is enforcing the law in force and the rulings of European courts,” digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said. “The transcription of foreign same-sex marriage certificates is and will remain legal,” he said, adding that 184 same-sex couples had so far had their foreign marriage certificates transcribed. Katarzyna Kotula, the government official responsible for equality issues, said the TK ruling on the issue of transcriptions “has no legal force whatsoever”. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. For a long time, the government refused to appoint new judges to the Constitutional Tribunal as the terms of the previous judges expired, with some vacancies remaining unfilled for over a year. In recent months, the government has resumed appointing new judges, but President Karol Nawrocki, an ally of PiS, is refusing to administer the oath of office to some of them. World.title: Residents oppose move to add Polish village to list of protected monuments
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A decision to designate a village as a protected monument has sparked fierce opposition from residents, who have vowed to “fight until the end” against measures they say will limit their ability to renovate and build on their properties. The village in question, Ostaszów in southwestern Poland’s Lower Silesia province, was established in 1936 by Nazi Germany as an agricultural settlement of around 42 farms. At the time, the region still belonged to Germany. The Lower Silesian Provincial Conservator of Monuments argues Ostaszów has “unique, homogeneous historical architecture” requiring state protection, but local officials say that the way the decision was made, despite opposition from residents, shows “the voice of local communities has no significance”. After World War Two, most of Lower Silesia, including the village, became part of Poland. The village’s architecture has remained largely unchanged, with its residential buildings connected to barns, forming unique cohesive farmstead units. Around 250 people live there. Earlier this year, the residents were told proceedings had begun to add the village to the register of protected monuments, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. The provincial conservator said on Friday it had reached a decision. “The unique, above-standard historical, scientific and artistic value of Ostaszów as a monument cannot be questioned,” it wrote in a statement. It noted that a study by a team working under the culture ministry had found that the village was the only preserved settlement of its kind in Lower Silesia. Residents and local officials said they planned to appeal against the decision, arguing it would create additional bureaucracy and interfere with property owners’ ability to decide on building and renovation work. “We have a years-long legal battle ahead of us, but we won’t give up. We will fight until the end. We believe that decisions about the 42 homes in Ostaszów should be made by their residents, not by harmful officials,” residents wrote in a statement quoted by the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “In a cardboard state, the voice of local communities has no significance – only orders and bans count. Our future is to be decided by a heartless official from [the Lower Silesian capital of] Wrocław who does not even have time to meet with the victims of his decisions,” said the village head, Sylwia Mazur. Wieś Ostaszów wpisana do rejestru zabytków. Mieszkańcy będą się odwoływaćhttps://t.co/ZxmH2lbHnb pic.twitter.com/cPdL73PXIH — Dzieje.pl (@dziejepl) July 26, 2026 The conservator noted, however, that until the appeals process is concluded, construction works cannot proceed. It added that it planned to cooperate with locals to “develop principles of renovation and investment procedures in accordance with the regulations on the protection of monuments”. It also urged residents not to spread “scandalous narratives” about the decision leading to an “open-air museum, the impossibility of renovation, and the blocking of investments”. It said other villages in Lower Silesia were subject to similar protections without hindering their development. Gazeta Wyborcza cited some residents saying that the launch of proceedings in January had already forced them to pause work on their properties. Others complained that the decision will increase renovation costs due to strict conservation requirements. The Opole Provincial Conservator of Monuments said that, as of 2021, some 86 villages across Poland had been added to the register of monuments because of their historic layouts. World.title: Poland enters race to host EU-backed AI gigafactory
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has joined the European Union’s plan to build artificial intelligence (AI) gigafactories with a view to hosting one of the bloc’s new computing centres. Deputy digital affairs minister Dariusz Standerski said Poland had completed a key legal step by joining the joint procurement process. The move enables Poland to bid for one of seven AI gigafactory projects planned under the EU programme, potentially attracting investment of more than 10 billion zloty (€2.3 billion) while giving businesses, researchers and public institutions access to advanced AI computing capacity. “On behalf of the Republic of Poland, I have signed the Joint Procurement Agreement, which means that Poland joins the AI gigafactory initiative,” Standerski told daily Rzeczpospolita. Under the proposed model, AI gigafactories will be designed, financed, built and operated by private consortia selected through a European tender organised by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). In the first procurement round, EuroHPC JU plans to select seven projects comprising four medium-scale facilities and three large-scale sites. Poland is bidding for a medium-scale project, which would initially provide computing capacity equivalent to at least 25,000 AI accelerators before expanding to at least 75,000. The EU and its member states will support the projects by committing to purchase computing services during the initial years of operation, providing demand certainty for investors. “Poland and the EU will each buy 17% of the power, and the remaining two thirds will be made commercially available by a private consortium; Poland will commit to purchasing its own pool for five years,” Standerski said. Standerski also told the newspaper that companies’ interest in the project is “enormous”. “This means that, from the very first day the gigafactory is operational, part of its computing capacity will already have been sold,” he added. Poland’s government will spend 1.9 billion zloty (€437 million) equipping the majority of schools with so-called AI labs before the start of the next school year. The money will fund laptops, AI software and interactive displays, among other equipment https://t.co/outNQIGCv0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Standerski said the government would not designate a site for the facility, with the final location to be determined by the winning consortium through the European procurement process. He said the government had previously identified 10 locations across Poland capable of hosting. Last week, the deputy minister also said Poland was preparing to sign an agreement with the Czech government, under which cooperation would involve mutual purchases of computing capacity between the two countries. He also said Lithuania had committed to a one-sided arrangement to buy computing power from a Polish AI gigafactory. Częstochowa will become the first city in Poland to use the Polish Large Language Model to support the use of AI in providing municipal services. It will help write letters, analyse inquiries from residents, and summarise long documents https://t.co/SLrmVg9VBz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2025 Earlier this month, Poland’s government approved a resolution enabling the country to participate in the European AI Gigafactory programme, committing more than 400 million zloty towards what the government says would be the largest computing centre in the country’s history. The government also pledged to purchase AI services worth €100 million between 2028 and 2033, with a matching contribution from the European Union. According to the government’s timetable, the European procurement process is expected to begin later this year. World.title: Poland asks US to extradite former minister Ziobro over criminal charges
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has formally asked the United States to detain and extradite former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro, who is wanted on multiple criminal charges. Ziobro, a senior figure in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, is accused of offences including leading an organised criminal group and abuse of office. Having previously fled Poland to Hungary, where Viktor Orbán’s government, an ally of PiS, granted him asylum, Ziobro arrived in the United States in May following a change of government in Budapest. Wniosek o ekstradycję podejrzanego Zbigniewa Ziobro: ⬇️https://t.co/YC7T3RrIEc — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) July 27, 2026 Ziobro served as justice minister in the PiS government from 2015 to 2023. Last year, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 26 crimes, including leading a criminal group and approving the unlawful purchase of Pegasus spyware. In October, parliament approved the lifting of Ziobro’s immunity from prosecution. By then, however, he had already travelled to Hungary, and in December he was granted political asylum by the Hungarian government. In February this year, Warsaw’s district court approved a request from prosecutors to place Ziobro in pretrial detention. That decision was needed in order for the authorities to issue domestic and European arrest warrants against the suspect. However, Ziobro’s lawyers appealed against the decision. While that appeal was waiting to be heard, Orbán lost power in Hungary and, as his successor Péter Magyar was being sworn in, Ziobro left the country and flew to the United States. In July, a Warsaw court rejected Ziobro’s appeal, opening the way for Poland to seek the politician’s extradition from the US. Ziobro has no valid travel documents after Poland cancelled his passports and Budapest revoked his refugee status. The extradition request covers 19 of the 26 offences listed in the indictment, the prosecutors said. The documents submitted include the final order for Ziobro’s detention, the indictment, a wanted notice and evidence supporting the case. The request will now be sent through diplomatic channels to the US Department of Justice, where it will be assessed to determine whether it meets the formal requirements of the Polish-US extradition treaty, prosecutor Anna Adamiak said. If the request satisfies those requirements, it will be referred to a US federal court, where a judge will decide on the legal admissibility of Ziobro’s extradition to Poland. A court has upheld a request by prosecutors to bring former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro, who is wanted on 26 criminal charges, into detention. The decision paves the way for Poland to request Ziobro's extradition from the US, where he fled in May https://t.co/vIPRjvgQnA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 2, 2026 Asked how long the extradition process could take, Adamiak said previous cases suggested proceedings could last anywhere from a few months to several years, depending on their nature and complexity. Adamiak noted, however, that the extradition proceedings would not determine Ziobro’s guilt. “Its role is merely to assess whether the surrender of that person in extradition proceedings is legally permissible in light of treaty regulations and domestic law,” she told reporters, quoted by online news service Wirtualna Polska. “However, the decision on surrender is, of course, a decision made by the state, so other circumstances may also play a role,” she added. PiS, Poland’s largest opposition party, enjoys close ties with US President Donald Trump’s administration. Poland's conservative opposition enthusiastically welcomed Trump's return to the White House, but it is becoming increasingly difficult for them to maintain a tough anti-Russian line while also showing allegiance to the US president, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/4PW6H9nMEF — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 7, 2025 Asked at a news conference about the likelihood of Ziobro’s extradition and when it might take place, Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the question should be directed at “the other Donald”, reported the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “We will, in accordance with the law, seek all available means to ensure that these politicians, against whom such serious charges have been brought, appear before a Polish court sooner or later,” he added. “We are waiting for positive signals from Washington. Will they come? I don’t know.” Ziobro has long denied all accusations, saying the case against him is an act of “political revenge” by Tusk’s government. Commenting on the extradition request on the conservative television channel Republika, Ziobro said he was pleased that the case would be heard “in the United States, on American soil, and before an American court”. He claimed that the proceedings would show that the Polish government “regularly breaks the law, ignores procedures, rejects democratic principles, has taken control of the prosecutor’s office unlawfully, and is trying to destroy the opposition”.
