Tech.title: Mac Mini Availability: Long Waits and Higher Prices
Tech.content:
Three months ago, outgoing Apple CEO Tim Cook admitted that the company had been caught off guard by the sharp increase in demand for the Mac Mini. Cook said it may take “several months” to catch up with demand, fueled by a boom in people using the compact computer for local AI workloads.

Now, while the situation has improved slightly, things are far from normal. At its worst, the base configuration of the Mac Mini was completely sold out on Apple’s storefront. This is true at third-party retailers like Amazon or Best Buy. Apple has them back in stock for a while now on Apple.com, but slow shipping times still show how dire the situation is.

Longer Waits

When buying directly from Apple, the cheapest Mac Mini with only 16 GB of RAM ships in three to four weeks. A MacBook Air from Apple with the same 16 GB of RAM configuration has a delivery window of two to three weeks—same as the MacBook Neo with 8 GB of RAM.

RAM is the primary contributing factor to the delays, as the waits get longer as capacity increases. Mac Mini configurations with 36 GB of RAM have wait times of around a month, while 48 GB of memory will take three months or longer to ship to customers. Meanwhile, a Mac Studio with 48 GB of memory takes an estimated “13 to 14 weeks” to arrive. That's an incredibly long time to wait. These higher-end memory configurations aren't even on offer at Amazon or Best Buy.

The wait times may put Apple in conflict with its next update of the Mac Mini and Mac Studio. Apple has not updated the Mac Mini since October 2024, but rumors have been pointing to an M5 chip update this fall. That means if you order an M4 Mac Mini right now, you could receive it after the newer model has been announced. That's how far behind Apple has become in meeting demand.

The fastest way to get a Mac Mini right now is through Amazon. While configuration options are limited, you can buy an M4 Mac Mini with 24 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage and have it shipped in just a few days. You'll be paying $1,570, which is $471 more than what the Apple Store is charging. You can also get the M4 Pro Mac Mini for $1,570, which is only $100 more than Apple's prices and delivers within a week and a half. These are really the only models I recommend buying at this point.

Even Higher Prices

Prices have increased across the board on all Macs. At the beginning of May, Apple quietly discontinued the starting configuration of the Mac Mini, which used to come with 256 GB of storage and cost $599. This meant the starting price for a Mac Mini immediately jumped to $799.

Skip ahead to the end of June, and the 256-GB configuration has been brought back for $100 more at $699 (while the 512-GB model is also now up $100 to $899), in line with the price increases made to MacBooks. But the Mac Studio is where things have become very expensive. The starting price of the M4 Max Mac Studio went up to $2,499, a $500 hike. The most powerful option, the M3 Ultra Mac Studio, went from $3,999 to $5,299. Not only are we still waiting months for these devices, but they now also cost up to 25 percent more.

When announced, these “unavoidable” price increases, as Apple called them, were blamed on the skyrocketing prices of components like memory and storage. Consumer memory prices started increasing rapidly through the end of 2025, and laptop manufacturers began warning investors of the shortage heading into 2026. Now, we're seeing the full picture of the effect on Apple's ability to keep prices down and meet demand.

Apple has reportedly been seeking alternative sources for memory components, such as previously blacklisted Chinese companies, but this is a long-term problem. Most industry forecasting says memory costs won't come down at least until 2030, and memory manufacturer SK Hynix recently stated that 2027 may end up being the “worst year” for the shortage. Buckle up.

Tech.title: Beef Experts Explain Why You Shouldn’t Default to the Grill When Cooking Steak
Tech.content:
Steak is simple enough, right? A hot cooking surface to sear the outside and some care taken not to overcook it. This formula works well enough for most cuts, but steak has more nuance than it seems. Various cuts with their specific fat content, marbling structure and thickness means there isn’t a one-size-fits-all method if you want professional-level results.

Will cooking your fat filet mignon on the grill render it inedible? No, but there are ideal processes for cook every type of steak. If you’ve spent good money on a pricey selection, you might want to consider learning them.

I turned to experts in the field for some advice on cooking steak. It turns out your grill, while good for some cuts, shouldn’t be the default for every piece of beef.

Best Meat Delivery Services for Quality Cuts All Summer See at CNET

Cooking steak well involves nuance — and plenty of pitfalls, depending on the cut, says Christopher Robert, executive chef at Queen Miami Beach. “Cooking the steak straight from the fridge and failing to let it rest afterward are the most common mistakes, and both stem from the same fundamental error: not respecting temperature.”

If you’d rather skip the fine print, a few basics will get you most of the way there for most cuts: start with clean grill grates, pat the meat dry, season generously, sear over high heat, and let it rest before cutting in.

But “most cuts” isn’t really the point here. What follows is a deeper dive into how chefs actually approach each type of steak — the small distinctions that separate a ribeye from a round, and that separate grill mastery from a solid effort.

Here is the best way to cook nine popular cuts of beef.

Ribeye: Wood fire

Ribeye does well when cooked over high heat, which makes wood-fired and pellet grills strong candidates. Traeger

Look, ribeye is the most universally revered grilling steak for a reason: Its extensive marbling and rich flavor are exactly what make you salivate when you hear the words “juicy steak.” But if you want to do it the most justice on the grill, forgo gas and charcoal and go with wood instead.

“I always start a ribeye over a real wood fire so I can get that high heat and build a deep, flavorful crust without overcooking the inside,” says Tucker Brown, a sixth-generation Texas rancher and ambassador for Beef. It’s What’s for Dinner. “I prefer wood over propane because it burns hotter and adds a natural smokiness that complements the richness of a ribeye in a way gas just can’t match.”

Best Pellet Grills for 2026 See at CNET

“The key is to let the steak sear over direct heat, then move it to a cooler spot to finish, so the marbling has time to render and keep the steak juicy,” he adds. “My favorite combination is a ribeye cooked over mesquite wood because it delivers an earthy flavor that holds its own with this rich cut of steak. Oak and hickory are also tasty options for a slightly milder smoke, and pecan can deliver a softer, subtly sweet profile.”

Flat iron: Hot and fast with compound butter

Hit a flat iron with compound butter before putting it on a hot grill. Getty Images

It bears mentioning that more than one chef profiled here gave props to the flat iron steak for being the most universally underrated.

“The flat iron steak has the most flavor and tenderness per dollar of any beef cut,” says Brad Baych, YouTube’s Butcher Wizard and author of Primal Cuts: A Butcher’s Guide to Selecting, Preparing, and Perfecting Beef. “It is found in the chuck, so it is automatically cheaper, but unlike other budget steaks, it is very tender. Because it is a thinner steak, it’s best cooked over open fire hot and fast, and lightly brushed with a little herb compound butter.”

On that note, not every steak can dance with compound butter on the grill and still be worth the effort. “Because it doesn’t have the ribeye’s fat running through it, it actually picks up a compound butter or a heavy herb crust in a way a ribeye never would,” says Katie Flannery, COO of Flannery Beef. “We’ll do garlic, thyme and good butter, and let it work into the meat before it hits the grill.”

Filet mignon: Dual zone, butter baste

Filet mignon is one of the more challenging steaks to cook. The chefs I spoke with recommend a dual-zone approach. Johnrob/Getty Images

From one of the cheapest cuts to the most expensive, “people always want to treat the filet like it’s precious, but the problem is it actually is,” says Flannery. “There’s no fat in that muscle to protect it, so a flare-up or 30 seconds of inattention and you’ve got a $40 piece of beef that chews like a sponge. What I do is use a two-zone fire and bring it up slowly on the cool side first, then sear it hard at the end.”

“Filet is naturally lean and a bit more subtle in flavor, so the mistake is treating it like a ribeye and expecting the same result,” says Jorge Thomas, founder of Swaledale Butchers. In addition to the dual-zone method that gives the filet the gentle treatment it wants, “a bit of butter, garlic and thyme at the end helps,” he says, “because filet wants a touch more added richness than some other steaks.”

Skirt: Score and add citrus

Try scoring skirt steak before slapping it on the grill. The Palmer/Getty Images

Skirt steak is a long, thin cut from the diaphragm muscle, meant to be cooked whole and sliced thin for fajitas or other preparations that call for thin-sliced steak. For its diva treatment, “I really enjoy scoring skirt steak, and then squeezing lime into the cuts,” says JD Alewine, owner and recipe developer of Them Bites in Asheville, North Carolina.

Scoring meat involves making thin slices that just scratch the surface, but they pay big dividends later on. “Scoring helps break down the long muscle fibers by cutting them into smaller sections when you cut against the grain,” says Alewine. “The lime acts like a marinade, and the acid helps to tenderize the meat. After you get a nice, quick char from high heat, let the steak rest, and hit it with lime again. It turns out perfect every time.”

T-bone: Grill position matters

When cooking a T-bone, place the tenderloin side further from the hottest area of the grill to keep it from overcooking. John Carlsen/CNET

Steaks on the bone have certain benefits, such as better moisture retention and richness, but also introduce complications. “When you’re cooking up a T-bone, think of it as cooking two different steaks at once,” says Joanne Gallagher, co-founder and recipe developer at Inspired Taste. “You’ll find the strip side is a lot firmer and fattier, and the tenderloin cooks faster and stays leaner.”

Two steaks in one is always a good time, but requires finesse. “Make sure you’re positioning the steak properly on the grill,” she says. “I’ll place the tenderloin side further from the hottest area of the grill to keep it from overcooking before the strip has a chance to develop a crust. Note that the bone will insulate the meat and slow cooking near the center, so you’ll want to give the steak a couple of extra minutes over indirect heat to help both sides finish evenly.”

Kebabs: Choose your meat and mind your tools

For the best kebabs, use slightly larger chunks of sirloin and marinate them in something sweet and spicy. Chowhound

Not every steak hits the grill whole, and kebabs are a welcome way to use bits and pieces from the butcher, especially when they’re on sale.

First, choose your fighter. “You want to use a hearty steak like sirloin for kebabs to ensure the meat cooks on par with any raw vegetables you may add, which traditionally can take more time to cook through,” says Jennifer Borchardt, culinary director of Pre Brands. “From a flavor profile, sirloin holds up to all different cuisines, so feel free to try them out with heavy marinades and seasonings.”

Also consider that skewers add a small degree of difficulty. “The trick with skewers is making sure you’re cooking each individual piece of meat evenly,” says Gallagher. “You’ll find the smaller pieces can overcook before the larger ones are done. To avoid this, I’ll use slightly larger chunks and then marinate them with something sweet and spicy. I’ll also leave little gaps in between each piece on the kebab so the heat can circulate around them to keep things cooking evenly.”

“For ideal kebabs, soak your skewers 30 minutes before cooking,” adds Borchardt, “and try them in a grill basket for an even cook.”

New York strip: Go cast iron and sear the fat cap

For strip steaks, consider pulling out the cast-iron skillet. Lodge

Sometimes, the best advice for a grilled steak is to bypass the grill and bring out your cast iron for the occasion. That doesn’t mean the grill won’t be involved, though. This just in: You can set your cast-iron skillet right on the grill next to your burgers and dogs for searing-hot heat.

“The New York strip is leaner than a filet and more flavorful than a tenderloin, and it’s my go-to premium steak cut because it has a great texture and flavor,” says Baych. No disrespect to the grill, “but they are best cooked in a cast iron pan. While your pan is heating up, sear just the fat cap,” he says, by holding the fatty edge of the steak directly on the skillet surface using tongs. “The fat renders, and then you’re cooking the steak in its own fat while keeping the cap crispy.”

Tri-tip: Mind the grain and go for a rub

A rub will do wonders for your tri-tip. Stefano Carocci/Getty Images

Adding to the list of underrated steaks, “I absolutely love tri-tip for grilling because it’s got a deep flavor similar to a roast, but still cooks nicely over live fire,” says Gallagher. “I’ve found that the secret is getting a good grasp on how the grain changes direction partway through the cut. You need to rotate it often, and once it’s off the grill, slice it into sections so each bite is as tender as possible.”

Because it’s got its own bold flavor that can take on other big flavors, “I’ll use a bolder seasoning rub for this cut, like a combination of dried dill, onion and garlic powder, Aleppo pepper, and coriander, among others,” she says. “A chimichurri sauce goes really well with tri-tip, too, because the herby flavor balances out the richness.”

Wagyu: Keep it cold and use the flat top

Wagyu wants a hot, flat surface, like cast iron or a scorching flat-top griddle. Vermont Wagyu

If you’ve sprung for Wagyu, you’re already going to have to break one of the cardinal rules that applies to basically every other kind of steak. “Grilling with Wagyu requires a slightly different approach than standard beef because of its exceptionally high omega-3 and omega-6 fat content and lower melting point,” says Sheila Patinkin of Vermont Wagyu. “Wagyu fat begins to melt at a much lower temperature than leaner beef, so steaks and patties should be kept in the fridge until the moment they hit the heat to preserve their structural integrity.”

Also, because the fat is kind of the point of Wagyu, putting them on a traditional grill is going to be an exercise in major flare-ups, where you effectively lose what you’ve paid for. To prevent this, “cook them on a flat top or cast-iron skillet,” says Patinkin, “rather than directly on grill grates.” Again, sometimes the best grilling advice is simply not to grill.

Tech.title: Private Claude Conversations Have Been Indexed by Search Engines
Tech.content:
Over the weekend, private Claude AI chats were made publicly accessible by search engines like Google and Bing, making for a privacy nightmare for the people involved and the chatbot’s maker, Anthropic.

Privacy concerns surrounding AI have always been around, but as these tools become more capable of pushing into your daily workflow with agentic capabilities, the threat of private data exposure is more timely than ever. This latest example shows that even simply sharing a conversation with others can get it exposed to a significantly larger audience.

This latest example shows that even simply sharing a conversation with others can get it exposed to a significantly larger audience.

Initially spotted by Reddit users, the common factor in the problem seems to be that the indexed conversations were shared — a common option within most AI chats — allowing “anyone with the link” to view what had been said in the Claude conversation itself.

This feature is apparently not completely protected from web crawlers, and personal conversations, while initially shared by users with people they chose, were exposed for the entire internet to see if one knew where to look.

Conversations indexed included medical records, sensitive personal information, internal corporate data and explicit content. They could be viewed within Google and Bing with a simple search and adding “site:claude.ai/share” to the query, yielding a trove of conversations, most of which have since been removed. Artifacts — tools, visualizations and shareable apps — were also accessible through search engines.

This isn’t the first time this has happened: Last year, Forbes reported the same thing happened with Anthropic — hundreds of conversations appeared on Google search results, only for them to be scrubbed later.

An Anthropic spokesperson told CNET that its system is working as it should and that when people decide to share their conversations, they’re making them publicly accessible.

“Shareable links are not guessable or discoverable unless people choose to share them themselves,” the spokesperson said. “When someone shares a conversation, they are making that content publicly accessible, and like other public web content, it may be archived by third-party services.”

Glenn Gabe, an SEO and AI search consultant at G-Squared Interactive, explained to CNET how this likely happened. It involves a .txt file called robots.txt, which is attached to web pages and tells search engines to crawl or not to crawl them to be indexed. Gabe says some companies don’t understand how Google and Bing treat URLs being blocked by robots.txt, despite Google’s developer documents explaining the functionality of the file.

“If you block Google or Bing from crawling your content, they can still index those URLs, just without crawling the content,” Gabe says. Without crawling a page’s content, search engines also can’t see any directives in the HTML. “That’s why noindexing URLs that are blocked by robots.txt doesn’t make any sense.”



Gabe says that if a company had public URLs — like shared Claude chats — Anthropic should “noindex” the content and not block crawling via robots.txt. That way, while the content would still be on the web, it wouldn’t be indexed by search engines, and only the people with the specific link would be able to find the shared chats.

If ever there were a good time to adjust your privacy settings and delete old conversations from your go-to AI chatbot, it’s now. To view your shared chats in Claude, you can go to Settings > Privacy > Shared Chats.

Tech.title: Gemini for MacOS Gets New Voice and ‘Screen Awareness’ Features
Tech.content:
Gemini users on MacOS are getting new voice capabilities, Google announced Wednesday. The app was released earlier this year and the tech giant has consistently added new features since its launch. The latest release will give you new ways to interact with Gemini using just your voice and a new screen awareness mode.

The Gemini app for MacOS is fairly feature-rich considering it’s only a couple of months old, and Google is continuing the feature push with the latest release. Pro and Ultra models have access to Gemini Spark, which can clean up your folders or reorganize things autonomously. You can also use them to create images or videos with just a couple of clicks.

One of the two new features in this release is intelligent dictation, which will transcribe words into polished text wherever your mouse cursor is and automatically remove your “ums” and “ahs.” The feature isn’t unlike what we saw with Android 17’s Rambler feature, which will automatically clean up text on the fly as you speak. Text dictation isn’t anything new at this point, but now there’s a Gemini AI-powered option that may make it more useful than ever.

The other new feature rolling out is a new Screen Awareness mode. This opt-in feature will allow Gemini to get a better understanding of what you’re working on by “seeing” what’s on your screen and active windows on your computer, so it can execute tasks on your behalf. Google gives the example of highlighting text inside a document and telling Gemini, “Turn these notes into an executive summary.” Gemini will then replace the highlighted text with the requested output.

The new voice capabilities are rolling out globally to all users of the Gemini app in English, with more languages to become available later this year.
